title: Invalid SAT model on Kakuro advanced-search profile
description: Background: The 2026-05-21 all-settings 300s retest found a reproducible invalid SAT model on profiling instance 5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7. The instance path is benchmarks/profiling/minisat-simp-five/5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7.cnf.xz. Default profile log/1.12a/profile-after-300-reopen and SAT_PHASE=saved log/1.12a/profile-300-phase-saved both solved the profiling suite without model failures, but every advanced setting tested printed s SATISFIABLE for this instance and failed the internal model checker. Affected artifacts: log/1.12a/profile-300-focused-vmtf/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-off/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-on/errors.log. Failure signature: SAT result requires model_check_result=pass, got fail; stdout s-line: s SATISFIABLE; internal model check failed. Settings that reproduced it: Focused/VMTF with SAT_PROFILE=experimental SAT_PROOF=drat SAT_SEED=0 SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved SAT_BINARY_FAST=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=basic SAT_VMTF=on SAT_REPHASE=off SAT_CHRONO=off; Stable-SAT rephase off with SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=recursive-limited SAT_REPHASE=off and otherwise same advanced flags; Stable-SAT rephase on with SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=recursive-limited SAT_REPHASE=on and otherwise same advanced flags. Observed times: Focused/VMTF ERROR at 47.321s, Stable-SAT rephase off ERROR at 46.886s, Stable-SAT rephase on ERROR at 47.183s. Goal: isolate the earliest responsible advanced feature interaction for this Kakuro invalid-model failure and provide a small, repeatable regression guard. Why it blocks progress: SAT model soundness is a solver contract, so no further Phase 1/Phase 2 tuning or promotion should proceed until this instance no longer returns an invalid SAT assignment under the advanced configs.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the Kakuro failure with at least one failing advanced config and record the exact command plus log path. Minimize the config matrix to identify whether the failure requires focused/stable mode, VMTF, SAT_BINARY_FAST, clause minimization, target/best phase, rephase, or a specific combination. Add a focused regression test or a benchmark guard command that fails before the fix and passes after it. Fix the root cause so the named instance either returns a SAT model that satisfies the original CNF or correctly returns another valid solver status; do not mask invalid SAT as UNKNOWN. Rerun the three failing advanced configs on this instance, default smoke, invariant smoke, cargo test, and a profile spot check. Acceptance requires no model-check failure on this instance, no default-profile status regression, and documentation of root cause in log/1.12a or the follow-up summary.
notes: Same root cause as SAT-playground-5b2.2.21 fixed Kakuro too. The binary-fast inline-abstraction migration failed to remap binary_clauses[*].clause_ref and binary_id_by_clause, so later GC could mark live binary clauses deleted and skip required binary implications. After adding remap_binary_clause_refs during inline abstraction migration, all three original Kakuro advanced failure configs were rerun at 120s and now return verified SAT instead of invalid SAT: focused/VMTF log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-focused-vmtf-120 result SAT ok 59.220s; stable rephase-off log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-stable-rephase-off-120 result SAT ok 61.993s; stable rephase-on log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-stable-rephase-on-120 result SAT ok 66.586s. Full validation also passed cargo fmt --check, cargo test -- --nocapture (240 passed), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, default smoke 9/9, invariant smoke 9/9, and default 300s profile 11/11 solved with no correctness failures at log/1.12a/profile-after-binary-remap-fix-300.
close_reason: Same binary-fast remap fix eliminates Kakuro invalid SAT model; all three original advanced configs now return verified SAT; full tests and default profile pass.

notes:

Initial plan: reproduce one failing advanced config, minimize the required flag combination, inspect the implicated search/propagation/model code, add or document a regression guard, fix root cause rather than masking invalid SAT, then rerun the REGRandom advanced configs plus Kakuro cross-check, smoke/invariant/cargo tests, and profile bench.
Reproduced and minimized failure. One-instance command env SAT_PROFILE=experimental SAT_PROOF=drat SAT_SEED=0 SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved SAT_BINARY_FAST=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=basic SAT_VMTF=on SAT_REPHASE=off SAT_CHRONO=off bash tools/bench.sh -t 60 -m 16384 -d /tmp/s11-regrandom-bench --log-dir log/debug-regrandom-focused-vmtf-60 solver/11-kissat-port returned ERROR in 9.531s with model_check_result=fail. The remap uses the same relocation table and helper as full GC, before replacing self.arena, so binary IDs remain stable while clause refs and binary_id_by_clause point at the migrated arena. Reviewed edge cases: deleted binaries remain deleted; binary reasons remain stable BinaryClauseId values and do not need reason rewrites; default profile is unaffected because SAT_BINARY_FAST defaults off; the regression test covers migration followed by GC and propagation of the preserved binary implication. Final validation: cargo fmt --check pass; cargo test -- --nocapture 240 passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass; default smoke 9/9; invariant smoke 9/9; default 300s profile log/1.12a/profile-after-binary-remap-fix-300 solved 11/11, PAR-2 631.032, no errors. compare_bench against log/1.12a/profile-after-300-reopen: verdict PASS, no status regressions, delta +6.224 PAR-2. compare_bench against log/profile-default-300-solver11-2026-05-21: verdict PASS, no status regressions, delta +3.453 PAR-2.
close_reason: Fixed binary-fast inline-abstraction remap bug; REGRandom invalid SAT model no longer reproduces under minimized or original advanced configs; full tests and default profile pass.

title: Fix advanced search SAT model-check failures
description: Background: 300s profile retesting for 1.12a showed that the default profile and SAT_PHASE=saved solve all 11 profiling instances correctly, but every advanced search setting tested can print s SATISFIABLE with an invalid model. Affected settings include Focused/VMTF, Stable-SAT rephase off, and Stable-SAT rephase on. The failures are reproducible in log/1.12a/profile-300-focused-vmtf/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-off/errors.log, and log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-on/errors.log. The failing instances are 46355da785714f239393e7630020cae3-REGRandom-K4-L1-Seed40.sanitized and 5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7. Goal: isolate which advanced component or interaction corrupts the final SAT assignment under these modes and fix it without regressing default or saved-phase behavior. Reasoning: performance tuning is irrelevant until SAT model validity is restored; the solver contract requires SAT models to satisfy the original CNF. Constraints: keep advanced features opt-in while debugging; preserve SAT Competition stdout/run.sh behavior; do not mask the issue by treating invalid SAT as UNKNOWN; keep proof behavior intact for UNSAT; record exact env configs and compare artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce both invalid-model failures with at least one advanced profile config and capture the failing command/log paths. Add a focused regression test or small reproducible benchmark guard when practical. Identify whether the root cause is focused/stable mode, VMTF, recursive clause minimization, binary-fast reason handling, target/best phase interaction, rephase, or a combination. Implement the fix and rerun cargo test, default smoke, invariant smoke, the failing advanced configs on the two named instances, and the relevant 300s profile/search-core spot checks. Acceptance requires no model-check failures for the advanced configs that previously failed, no default-profile status regression, and updated summary notes explaining the root cause and remaining performance status.
notes:
Discovered during 2026-05-21 all-settings retest for SAT-playground-5b2.2.16. This bead is a correctness blocker for promoting or further tuning the advanced search stack; it does not require promoting the advanced modes after correctness is fixed.
Blocking policy added 2026-05-21: this bug is now a P0 progress blocker. Do not start Phase 1 throughput/chrono work, Phase 1 promotion, Phase 2 inprocessing, or advanced-search milestone closure until the invalid SAT model failures are resolved or deliberately superseded with explicit user approval. The issue is not a performance miss: the advanced modes printed s SATISFIABLE while tools/bench.sh rejected the returned assignment against the original CNF. Default profile and SAT_PHASE=saved passed the same 300s profiling suite without model failures, so the failure appears tied to the composed advanced stack rather than the base solver/harness.
Resolved by the binary-fast inline-abstraction metadata remap fix from SAT-playground-5b2.2.21/SAT-playground-5b2.2.22. Root cause: SAT_BINARY_FAST metadata was not remapped when ensure_original_clause_abstractions rebuilt the arena for large formulas, so later GC could mark live binary clauses deleted and propagation missed original binary implications. Evidence: REGRandom minimized SAT_BINARY_FAST=on reproducer now UNSAT ok in 28.710s; all three REGRandom original advanced configs are clean 120s timeouts with no model error; all three Kakuro original advanced configs now return verified SAT in 59.220s, 61.993s, and 66.586s. Full validation passed fmt, cargo test 240, clippy, default smoke, invariant smoke, and default 300s profile 11/11 solved PAR-2 631.032 with compare_bench PASS/no status regressions against prior 300s runs. Remaining advanced-search performance regressions are promotion/tuning issues, not this correctness blocker.
close_reason: Resolved binary-fast metadata remap soundness bug; both concrete invalid-model blockers are closed and all previously failing advanced configs on REGRandom/Kakuro no longer produce model-check failures.

title: Replace SAT_VMTF=single guards with Kissat focused-mode VMTF parity
description: Follow-up to SAT-playground-egy. The current SAT_VMTF=single profile was made benchmark-safe with fixed conflict/decision/propagation budgets and a medium-formula phase guard, but that is not how Kissat makes VMTF safe. Kissat uses VMTF only while solver->stable is false (focused mode): decide.c chooses last_enqueued_unassigned_variable in focused mode and largest_score_unassigned_variable in stable mode; bump.c moves analyzed variables to the VMTF queue front only in focused mode and bumps VSIDS scores only in stable mode. The stabilizer is the focused/stable execution model around VMTF, not standalone numeric VMTF guards. Kissat also resets mode averages at switches, uses focused conflicts and stable search_ticks for mode limits, updates target/best phases only in stable mode, uses target phase in focused mode only when target > 1, and applies mode-specific restart trail reuse. Rework the solver 11 VMTF path so the default-safe route is Kissat-style focused-mode VMTF parity, then remove or demote the arbitrary SAT_VMTF=single guard path from any promoted profile.
acceptance_criteria: Document the exact Kissat source references and current solver divergence in the bead notes or implementation log. Replace the promoted VMTF approach with focused/stable parity: VMTF decisions and move-to-front bumps only in focused mode, VSIDS heap decisions and score bumps in stable mode, mode switch scheduling through the existing SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS path or a corrected successor, Kissat-compatible phase update/use semantics, and restart trail reuse evaluated per mode. Remove, hide, or clearly mark the fixed SAT_VMTF=single budget/formula guards as experimental fallback rather than a promoted solver policy. Add unit tests covering focused-mode VMTF activation, stable-mode VSIDS activation, mode-switch queue/heap invariants, and phase behavior. Run cargo test, default/invariant smokes, SAT_VMTF/focused-stable smokes, and a 300s/16GiB benchmarks/profiling comparison against default, the current guarded SAT_VMTF=single result, and solver10. No UNKNOWN/timeout/error row may replace a SAT/UNSAT baseline solve.

title: Implement formula classification (binary fraction, size) for adaptive feature policy
description:
Task class: meta-policy / adaptive configuration. Implements kissat-style formula classification that routes runtime feature selection per-instance.

Background: Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/classify.c) computes two classification flags after preprocessing:
- solver->classification.small: clauses <= GET_OPTION(smallclauses)
- solver->classification.bigbig: binary_clauses / total_clauses >= bigbigfraction (default 99% per mille)

These flags are then read across the solver to switch policy (different reduce schedule, different restart trigger, etc).

Solver 11 has no formula classification. Every instance gets the same policy. The third-pass investigation (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md, Gap 12) found that the BEST kissat-feature config in solver 11 is DRAMATICALLY per-instance:
- VMTF wins mp1 (43x), battleship (25x) but TIMES OUT on sudoku/REGRandom
- binary_fast wins case9 (4.6x), REGRandom (2.2x) but breaks mp1 and battleship  
- inblock minimization wins Kakuro (4x), Iter30 (1.3x) but breaks battleship/case9
- chrono helps mp1, Kakuro, velev but hurts REGRandom

Combination experiments (S1-S7) confirmed features ANTAGONIZE each other. The 'kitchen sink' S7 config loses on every instance vs the best per-instance config.

Without classification, solver 11 cannot route to the right policy. This is the deepest structural mismatch from the third-pass investigation: solver 11 has the FEATURES but not the ADAPTIVE SCHEDULER.

Proposed change: implement classify() that runs after preprocessing and before main search loop. Compute:
- formula_size_class: small / medium / large (clauses < 10k, 10k-1M, > 1M)
- binary_fraction: binary_clauses / total_clauses
- avg_clause_size: total_literals / total_clauses
- variable_density: total_literals / vars

Store as a formula_class field on the solver. Then:
- Add policy-selector functions that consult formula_class
- Initial routing rule (from third-pass data): if binary_fraction > 0.6 and small formula, enable VMTF + binary_fast; if large UNSAT random pattern, prefer A_default policy; etc.
- Routing decisions logged via SAT_STATS_JSON

Implementation notes:
- One-shot classification, not periodic.
- Hardcode routing rules initially; the rules can be tuned empirically.
- Future: dynamic re-classification after inprocessing rounds.

Tests:
  test_classify_small_formula_routes_to_vmtf
  test_classify_random_3sat_routes_to_baseline
  test_classify_logs_class_decision_in_stats

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows aggregate PAR-2 improvement when adaptive policy is enabled vs static A_default, with no instance regression > 20%.

Larger project role: closes Gap 12 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Required prerequisite for safely defaulting any kissat-style feature that helps some instances and hurts others. Most direct path to making solver 11 beat A_default on the 10-instance profiling suite.

title: Allow VMTF branching in single-mode (not just focused-stable)
description:
Task class: branching heuristic activation. Enables solver 11 to use VMTF without requiring the focused-stable mode scaffolding that itself regresses the suite.

Background: VMTF (Variable Move To Front) is currently gated by THREE conditions in vmtf_branching_active (solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:2863-2867):
1. self.vmtf_queue.is_some()
2. self.search_mode_policy == SearchModePolicy::FocusedStable
3. self.search_mode == SearchMode::Focused

Config-time validation in config.rs:1109 also enforces: 'SAT_VMTF=on requires SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable'.

This is overly strict. Kissat's bump.c:103-112 makes VMTF the unconditional focused-mode branching heuristic — but kissat's focused mode itself is just one half of always-running mode alternation. In solver 11, focused-stable mode alternation is broken (G_focused_stable solves only 5/10, log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/FINDINGS.md), so requiring focused-stable as a prerequisite for VMTF traps users between two failure modes.

Evidence from third-pass investigation (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md):
- I_vmtf_only (focused-stable + VMTF) solves mp1 in 1.5s, battleship in 0.9s, Kakuro in 63s, velev in 38s — dramatic wins on SAT-leaning instances
- But same config TIMES OUT on sudoku and REGRandom (the focused-stable mode penalty)
- The wins come from VMTF specifically, not focused-stable. M_chrono_only (no VMTF, no focused-stable) solves all 10 in +19% PAR-2.
- mp1 is THE canonical case: VSIDS-only takes 47s; VMTF takes 1.5s — 31x speedup just from the branching heuristic.

Proposed change: introduce SAT_VMTF=single|focused-only|off (default off) and decouple VMTF activation from search_mode_policy:
- 'single': VMTF active for the whole single-mode search (no focused-stable required)
- 'focused-only' (current behavior): VMTF only in focused-stable + Focused mode
- 'off' (current default): VSIDS only

Implementation notes:
- src/main.rs:2863 vmtf_branching_active gains a branch for single-mode VMTF
- src/main.rs:3934 pick_branch_lit needs to ensure VMTF queue is initialized in single mode
- Need to maintain VMTF queue (link/stamp updates) even when search_mode_policy=Single
- Config validation in config.rs:1109 should accept SAT_VMTF=single without requiring SAT_SEARCH_MODE
- Tests should cover both single-mode VMTF and focused-stable VMTF paths

Tests:
  test_vmtf_single_mode_activates_without_focused_stable
  test_vmtf_single_mode_solves_mp1_faster_than_vsids
  test_vmtf_queue_updated_in_single_mode

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows mp1 solves < 10s under SAT_VMTF=single (down from 47s under A_default), with no new timeouts on the 10-instance suite.

Larger project role: closes Gap 5 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Unblocks VMTF wins on mp1 (43x), battleship (25x), Kakuro (4x), velev (2x) without the focused-stable mode regressions. Required prerequisite for SAT-leaning per-instance configs.

title: Implement kissat lucky-assignment heuristic before main search
description:
Task class: pre-search optimization. Implements kissat's lucky.c pre-search heuristic which catches trivially-SAT instances in O(VARS).

Background: kissat's kissat_lucky (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/lucky.c:307) runs before AND after preprocessing (search.c:184-189, gated by luckyearly=1 and luckylate=1 — both default ON). It tries assigning ALL variables to one polarity (true, then false, then 'backward setting') with bounded UP-propagation. If UP completes without conflict, the model is found.

Solver 11 has no lucky pass — search starts immediately after preprocessing with all phases at FALSE (initial_phase). Battleship-16-31-sat is a textbook lucky case: kissat solves it in 0.18s, solver 11 default takes 23.5s (130× slower), and solver 11's best config (S6_vmtf_otfs) takes 0.95s (5× slower than kissat).

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 6. Per-instance lookup table shows battleship is the canonical lucky case: kissat 0.18s, solver 11 A_default 23.5s, solver 11 S6_vmtf_otfs 0.95s.

Proposed change: add a SAT_LUCKY=on flag (default-on-but-opt-out for safety initially) that calls a lucky() method between BVE preprocessing and the main CDCL search loop. The lucky() method:
1. Snapshot current assignment, level 0.
2. Try all-true assignment (assume positive literal of every unassigned var); UP-propagate. If no conflict and trail==num_vars → SAT.
3. Backtrack, try all-false. Same check.
4. Backtrack, try 'backward' pattern (positive then negative alternating).
5. If any succeeded, write the model and exit with SAT.
6. Otherwise restore state and fall through to CDCL.

Implementation notes:
- Place in src/main.rs alongside other pre-search code (~line where preprocessing finishes).
- Probably needs a guarded version of propagate() that doesn't update activity scores or restart EMAs.
- Should run after preprocessing so it sees the simplified formula.
- Add a stats counter lucky_attempts/lucky_solved.

Tests:
  test_lucky_all_true_solves_horn_sat
  test_lucky_all_false_solves_dual_horn
  test_lucky_does_not_change_state_when_fails

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows battleship-16-31-sat solves in < 5s under default config (down from 23.5s).

Larger project role: closes Gap 6 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Low risk because failed lucky calls just continue to normal search. May rescue several SAT-leaning instances in the broader 100-instance suite where kissat solves in < 1s.

title: Reduce MAX_USED_RECENTLY from 3 to 2 to cure lbd-tiered learned-DB bloat
description:
Task class: solver-behavior tuning. One-line constant change in src/main.rs that recovers the lbd-tiered DB-bloat slowdown identified by the 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes investigation.

Background: src/main.rs:140 sets `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 3;`. This value is the initial `used_recently` counter assigned to every newly learned clause in `initialize_learnt_lbd` (src/main.rs:2174). The lbd-tiered reduce loop ages this counter down by 1 each pass (`age_learned_clause_on_reduce`, src/main.rs:5229-5243). A tier-1 or tier-2 candidate is only deletable when `used_recently == 0` (`reduce_candidate`, src/main.rs:5099-5119), so with MAX=3 every fresh clause survives at least 3 reduce passes regardless of LBD or usage. Combined with the sub-linear `learned_lit_budget` schedule (`refresh_learned_lit_budgets`, src/main.rs:4394 = `LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_BASE + LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_FACTOR * sqrt(reductions)`), this produces monotonic DB growth that bloats `learned_clauses_final` 3x-13x versus the legacy reducer, slows per-propagation throughput 2.0x-3.1x, and is the dominant mechanism behind the kissat-feature regression on the random profile-suite instances.

Investigation evidence: `/home/bojji/code/SAT-playground/log/kissat-investigation-findings-2026-05-23.md` (root-cause decomposition) and `/home/bojji/code/SAT-playground/log/kissat-investigation-experiment-2026-05-23.md` (4-variant knob sweep). Per-instance and aggregate numbers below come directly from those runs.

Proposed change: `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 2;`

Knob sweep (E_lbd_ema_tiered config, 6 profiling instances, 120s timeout, PAR-2 with 240s/TO):

| Variant | MAX | BUDGET_FACTOR | solved | PAR-2  | delta vs V0 |
|---------|-----|---------------|--------|--------|-------------|
| V0      | 3   | 300           | 5/6    | 318.85 | --          |
| V1      | 1   | 300           | 5/6    | 315.06 | -1.2%       |
| V2      | 1   | 100           | 5/6    | 313.23 | -1.8%       |
| V3      | 2   | 300           | 5/6    | 294.43 | -7.7%       |

V3 (MAX=2) is the recommended knob value. V1 (MAX=1) is too aggressive on the structured-SAT win cases: it pushes feistel_b64_k32_r22 from 21.08s (V0) to 50.13s (V1, +138%) because clauses get aged out before they have time to mature into useful reasons. V3 gives every fresh clause one extra reduce-pass of protection, which preserves the structured-SAT wins while still aging out the random-noise clauses. Tightening LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_FACTOR (V2) only moves the needle 12% on one instance and is NOT the dominant lever.

V3 vs V0 on E_lbd_ema_tiered per-instance (s):

| instance              | V0     | V3     | ratio |
|-----------------------|--------|--------|-------|
| feistel_b64_k32_r22   | 21.08  | 24.68  | 1.17x | (only regression)
| feistel_b64_k52_r17   | 19.34  |  9.28  | 0.48x |
| feistel_b64_k57_r18   |  2.66  |  2.39  | 0.90x |
| random_v285_s2        | 10.68  |  6.77  | 0.63x |
| random_v292_s4        | 25.08  | 11.31  | 0.45x |
| random_v355_s3        |   TO   |   TO   |  --   | (separate problem — see below)

Mechanism confirmation (V3 vs V0 on E_lbd_ema_tiered, per-instance stats):

- feistel_b64_k52_r17: conflicts 273k -> 176k (0.64x), props/sec 1.90M -> 2.62M (1.38x), DB unchanged.
- random_v285_s2: conflicts 467k -> 324k (0.69x), props/sec 2.02M -> 2.18M (1.08x), DB 23007 -> 19321 (0.84x).
- random_v292_s4: conflicts 992k -> 514k (0.52x), props/sec 1.84M -> 2.11M (1.15x), DB 26286 -> 24884 (0.95x).
- feistel_b64_k32_r22: conflicts 343k -> 444k (1.29x, the cost), props/sec 2.67M -> 2.92M (1.09x), DB 44526 -> 40626 (0.91x).

V3 improves both axes (work x speed) on every instance except feistel_b64_k32_r22, where work increases by 29%. The +17% feistel_b64_k32_r22 regression is the documented cost.

A_default config is unaffected by this knob (the constant only matters when ReducePolicy::LbdTiered is selected). Sanity-checked: V0/V1/V2/V3 A_default rows are within 1% across all 6 instances.

Implementation:

1. Change one constant in solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:140:
   - `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 3;` -> `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 2;`
2. Existing tests at src/main.rs:7588-7590 assert `MAX_USED_RECENTLY` literally on three tier checks; they will still pass because they use the constant by name.
3. No config-schema change required (the constant is not currently exposed via SAT_*).

Tests:
- existing test_lbd_*_initial_used_recently family must continue to pass.
- bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port — 8/8 expected.
- SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port — 8/8 expected.

Benchmark gate (must run before promotion):
- bash tools/bench.sh -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port (default profile, no env override). Must remain PASS vs the most recent default-profile baseline (no solved-row regression).
- Same command with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_STATS_JSON=on. Expected per the experiment: PAR-2 improves by ~24s on the 6 profiling instances. Watch the random_v355_s3 row — it remains TIMEOUT after this change.

Risk IDs: R3 (learned-clause correctness via aggressive eviction), R5 (search trajectory). Rollback: restore MAX_USED_RECENTLY to 3.

Out of scope (separate beads):
- random_v355_s3 TIMEOUT under E_lbd_ema_tiered persists after this change. Mechanism is EMA-restart trajectory, NOT DB bloat (V1, V2, V3 all shrink DB and still time out; D_lbd_tiered alone — Luby + lbd-tiered — also times out). Track separately.
- SAT-playground-5b2.2.44 (tier-2 evictable when !over_budget) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.49 (histogram bias audit) touch adjacent reduce_candidate code. They should be re-evaluated after this change lands because the smaller steady-state DB changes the tier distribution.

Reproduction (in worktree): /tmp/sat-analysis-kissat/log/kissat-investigation/exp/run_experiment.sh sweeps V0/V1/V2/V3 across the 6 profiling instances. Source files for the 4 variants are at /tmp/sat-analysis-kissat/solver/11-kissat-port/target/release/sat-solver-{v0,v1,v2,v3} (built in that worktree).
acceptance_criteria: MAX_USED_RECENTLY constant changed from 3 to 2. cargo test + smoke + lbd-tiered smoke all PASS. tools/bench.sh on benchmarks/profiling: no solved-row regression in default profile, ~7% PAR-2 improvement in SAT_USE_LBD+SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema+SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered profile. feistel_b64_k32_r22 +17% regression on E_lbd_ema_tiered documented in README. random_v355_s3 timeout under kissat features tracked as separate bead.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 investigation. Empirical evidence: log/kissat-investigation-findings-2026-05-23.md + log/kissat-investigation-experiment-2026-05-23.md. 4-variant knob sweep ran on 6 profiling instances at 120s timeout.
s11-02: Claimed after completing 1.14g OTFS because bv/bd now surface this as the highest-priority executable Phase 1 bead. Using existing 1.14g gated-off profile as the before point for lbd-tiered/recursive-min profile where applicable.
s11-02: Rejected/reverted for this grouping. MAX_USED_RECENTLY=2 passed unit/smoke checks but failed the required 11-instance 300s lbd-tiered profile mode used in this session: baseline MAX=3 log/phase1/1.14g-otfs-profile-after-gated-off solved 10/11, PAR-2 1131.774; MAX=2 log/phase1/1.14g-1.14x-max-used-recently-profile-after solved 10/11, PAR-2 1253.070 (+121.296). It solved mp1-Nb7T46 (TIMEOUT -> SAT 173.98s) but regressed random_v355_s3 (SAT 62.49s -> TIMEOUT), and REGRandom-K4 slowed 95.99s -> 129.11s. Reverted code/docs to MAX=3 and left bead open for a narrower E_lbd_ema_tiered-only evaluation or alternative guard.
s11-02: Rejection summary artifact recorded at log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-rejected-summary.md.
s11-02 retry: Reclaimed for explicit on/off benchmarking in the bead's intended key modes. Baseline/off will use current MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3. On-change will use MAX_USED_RECENTLY=2. Primary key mode: SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_STATS_JSON=on over benchmarks/profiling with 300s/16GiB. Default profile will be used as sanity/no-regression check.
s11-02 retry off/key baseline complete: log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-retry-off-key, settings SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_STATS_JSON=on SAT_TRACE_FULL=on, 11 profiling instances, 300s, 16GiB. MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3 solved 9/11 (5 SAT + 4 UNSAT), timeouts mp1-Nb7T46 and random_v355_s3, PAR-2 1823.076.
s11-02 retry complete/rejected: In the bead's intended key mode (SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_STATS_JSON=on SAT_TRACE_FULL=on, 11 profiling instances, 300s/16GiB), MAX_USED_RECENTLY=2 regressed versus MAX=3. Off MAX=3 log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-retry-off-key solved 9/11, PAR-2 1823.076. On MAX=2 log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-retry-on-key solved 9/11, PAR-2 1885.953 (+62.877). Wins: REGRandom -51.985s, random_v292 -13.855s, feistel_k52 -9.972s. Regressions: Kakuro +124.732s, Sudoku +12.453s, feistel_k32 +3.642s. mp1 and random_v355 remained TIMEOUT. Reverted to MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3. Summary artifact: log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-key-retry-summary.md. Final checks after revert: cargo test used_recently, cargo test lbd_tiered, cargo test, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, default smoke, and key-mode smoke all passed.
Deep investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 1 Gap 3) reframes this bead's recommendation.

Reading kissat source (learn.c:110, deduce.c:18, reduce.c:70-72) shows kissat uses a 5-bit used counter (MAX_USED=31) and sets c->used = MAX_USED on every learn or reason use. Solver 11 uses MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3 and bumps to max(used, 1) on reason use — a 50% protection for re-used clauses vs kissat's full reset.

The proposed MAX=3->2 change tightens fresh-clause aging by 33% but tightens reused-clause aging by 50% — a non-uniform shrink that doesn't match kissat semantics. This is why the 11-instance suite test rejected it: it hits the wrong quantity.

Correct semantic fix is split into a new bead (SAT-playground-ycw, 'Fix mark_learned_clause_recent bump semantics to match kissat'). That bead changes mark_learned_clause_recent to set used = MAX_USED_RECENTLY on reason use, AND optionally widens MAX_USED_RECENTLY toward kissat's 31 (7 or 15 as a first step).

Recommendation: close this bead once SAT-playground-ycw lands. The 'reduce MAX 3->2' direction is wrong; the 'bump-to-MAX on use AND widen MAX' direction is right.
close_reason: Superseded by SAT-playground-ycw. The MAX_USED_RECENTLY 3->2 direction was rejected twice (log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-rejected-summary.md and log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-key-retry-summary.md) on the broader profiling suite. The third-pass investigation (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md) and DEEPER_FINDINGS.md identified the correct fix as changing mark_learned_clause_recent's bump semantics from max(used,1) to MAX_USED_RECENTLY (matching kissat's c->used=MAX_USED). That work continues under SAT-playground-ycw with the correct dimension.

title: Investigate solver11 normalised-instance memory aborts
description: Milestone M.2 discriminating run log/M.2/discriminating-2026-05-19-01 found solver/11-kissat-port aborting with exit 134 on large normalised SAT instances under the standard 16 GB memory gate. 83aa254f-1.normalised failed with 'memory allocation of 128 bytes failed' and missing result.json; an isolated solver10 comparison from log/bench-s11-1.3a-83aa-solver10-2026-05-19-1721 showed the same 83aa failure, so that case is pre-existing. ee5fb3e-11.normalised failed with 'memory allocation of 2589149280 bytes failed' and missing result.json and was not previously isolated. Goal: reproduce both failures, identify whether allocation pressure comes from preprocessing, search, proof/output, clause DB/GC, or decompression/harness behavior, and decide whether solver11 should return UNKNOWN with a valid result contract under SAT_LIMIT_RSS_MB/ulimit instead of aborting. notes: s11-01 result (2026-05-20): Reproduced both target aborts under bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384. title: [0.12] Add solver 10 vs 11 overhead regression gate
description:
Background:
The profiling comparison initially showed solver 11 PAR-2 712.310 vs solver 10 PAR-2 704.278 on the 120s profiling set, with identical solved/timeout outcomes but +8.032s solved-runtime delta. Interleaved repeats confirmed the overhead is real. This needs a repeatable gate so future agents do not reintroduce Section 0 instrumentation overhead or misread one-off benchmark noise.

Goal and intent:
Create a lightweight, repeatable overhead regression gate specifically for baseline solver 10 vs solver 11 parity. This gate should be cheap enough to run before Phase 1 performance work and precise enough to separate search-path changes from local overhead.

Implementation guidance:
- Add a script such as tools/ci_solver11_overhead.sh or extend existing CI tooling with an explicit overhead mode.
- Build solver/10-bve-preprocess and solver/11-kissat-port once in release mode.
- Run interleaved repeats with alternating order to avoid sequential thermal/cache bias.
- Include at least feistel_b64_k57_r18.cnf and random_v285_s2.cnf, because both are ~8s and confirmed the overhead signal.
- Record mean, median, per-run times, statuses, proof setting, and environment.
- For at least one representative instance, compare search counters to confirm identical conflicts/decisions/propagations/restarts when asserting overhead rather than search-path drift.
- Make the threshold configurable, but default to flagging/failing above <=1.5% median overhead after 0.10/0.11 have landed.

Constraints and considerations:
- Keep this gate separate from broad benchmark speed claims. It measures infrastructure overhead, not solver strength.
- Do not require perf hardware counters because this environment has perf_event_paranoid=4.
- The script should leave artifacts under log/ with enough detail for bead comments and future analysis.
- It may run fewer repeats in regular fast CI and more repeats when invoked explicitly.

Testing expectations:
- Validate the script detects the current known overhead before fixes, or records expected-fail semantics until 0.10/0.11 close.
- After 0.10/0.11, the gate should pass with the accepted threshold.
- Run ci_solver11_fast and the new overhead gate before closing.

How this serves the larger project goal:
This gives future solver work a stable performance baseline. Without it, later algorithmic changes could be judged against a moving baseline contaminated by instrumentation overhead.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible overhead-gate script or documented CI command runs interleaved solver 10/solver 11 repeats on representative profiling instances, records status/search-counter parity, reports mean and median deltas, and fails or clearly flags when default solver 11 overhead exceeds the accepted threshold; gate passes after 0.10/0.11 fixes and blocks M.1/Phase 1 until then.
notes:
Started 2026-05-19 after 0.10, 0.11, and 0.13 closed. bv now lists this as the next ready executable Section 0 bead. Plan is to add a lightweight overhead gate that builds solver 10/11, runs interleaved alternating-order repeats on the Feistel and random profiling instances, records log artifacts with per-run/mean/median/status/counter parity, and fails when solver 11 median overhead exceeds the default threshold.
Implemented and reviewed solver 10 vs solver 11 overhead regression gate.

Code changes:
- Added tools/ci_solver11_overhead.sh as the user-facing entry point.
- Added tools/ci_solver11_overhead.py to build solver/10-bve-preprocess and solver/11-kissat-port once, run alternating-order interleaved timing repeats, write per-run stdout/stderr/status artifacts, summarize mean/median deltas, and fail if solver 11 median overhead exceeds the configurable threshold.
- Default gate settings: 3 repeats, 120s per run, default SAT_PROOF behavior for timing, 1.5% median solver 11 overhead threshold, instances benchmarks/profiling/feistel_b64_k57_r18.cnf and benchmarks/profiling/random_v285_s2.cnf.
- Added a counter-parity phase using SAT_PROOF=off and SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL=1000000000 on the Feistel instance. It parses final c search done counters and requires matching result, conflicts, decisions, propagations, and restarts.
- Artifacts are written under log/solver11-overhead-<timestamp>/ with config.json, runs.csv, summary.json, build logs, timing stdout/stderr files, and counter-parity stdout/stderr files. Large proof files are removed from per-run output directories after status capture.
- Added tools/ci_solver11_overhead.py to tools/ci_solver11_fast.sh py_compile coverage.

- Reviewed alternating order and confirmed repeat 1/3 run solver10 then solver11 while repeat 2 reverses the order.
- Reviewed failure modes: nonzero rc, timeout, status mismatch, threshold breach, or missing/mismatched search-counter parity fails the gate.
- Added a robustness fix so custom log dirs or instances outside the repo still print usable artifact paths instead of crashing on relative_to.
- Verified shell wrapper remains small and shellcheck-compatible; bash -n passes.

Validation:

- bash -n tools/ci_solver11_overhead.sh tools/ci_solver11_fast.sh: passed

  - feistel_b64_k57_r18.cnf: median10 8.504314s, median11 8.433206s, median delta -0.836%, mean delta -0.944%, all SATISFIABLE, status_ok true
  - random_v285_s2.cnf: median10 8.386782s, median11 8.329535s, median delta -0.683%, mean delta -0.651%, all UNSATISFIABLE, status_ok true

title: [0.10] Remove always-on hot-path stats overhead
description:
Background:
Section 0 added rich JSON stats and hot-path propagation counters to solver/11-kissat-port. Interleaved confirmation after Section 0 showed the overhead is real, not just sequential benchmark noise:
- feistel_b64_k57_r18, 5 interleaved repeats, default proof: solver 10 mean 8.497s, solver 11 mean 8.828s, +3.90%; median +3.84%.
- random_v285_s2, 5 interleaved repeats, default proof: solver 10 mean 8.394s, solver 11 mean 8.799s, +4.83%; median +4.55%.
- With SAT_PROOF=off, overhead persisted: feistel median +4.38%, random median +5.11%.
- Solver 11 JSON stats on feistel showed the same search work as solver 10 trace output: conflicts=551925, decisions=679410, propagations=43725178, restarts=1149. This points to per-operation overhead rather than a changed search trajectory.

Observed likely root cause:
solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs::propagate increments diagnostic counters on every watcher scan, blocker hit, stale skip, clause load, and binary/long implication. On feistel_b64_k57_r18, solver 11 reported watch_scans=576422300, watch_blocker_hits=344181851, watch_clause_loads=232240338, binary_props=4615846, long_props=42267146. These counters are currently updated even when SAT_STATS_JSON=off and tracing is off, adding hundreds of millions of extra hot-path stores.

Goal and intent:
Keep Section 0 observability, but make the default solver 11 hot path effectively solver-10-equivalent when diagnostic hot counters are not requested. Future Phase 1 algorithm work must not start from a baseline that is already 4-5% slower from instrumentation.

Implementation guidance:
- Introduce a stats/diagnostics mode that distinguishes always-required core counters from optional hot diagnostic counters.
- Keep core counters needed for correctness, trace summaries, and benchmark status, but gate high-frequency counters such as watch_scans, watch_blocker_hits, watch_clause_loads, watch_stale_skips, binary_props, and long_props behind an explicit config flag or compile-time specialization.
- Prefer a low-overhead design: const generic propagation helper, split fast/diagnostic propagation paths, or another pattern that lets the compiler remove diagnostic increments from the default path.
- Preserve JSON schema compatibility. When hot diagnostics are disabled, emit an explicit hot_diagnostics_enabled field or document zero/null semantics.
- Do not remove the ability to collect these counters for profiling/debugging.

Constraints and considerations:
- Do not silently drop stats fields used by tooling; update validators/tests if semantics change.
- Default behavior should remain SAT Competition compatible and proof/model correct.
- Avoid adding branches inside inner watcher loops if the branch still costs materially at scale.
- Compare default profile against solver 10 with the same proof setting and same run.sh path.

Testing expectations:
- Add unit tests or integration tests for the new stats mode/config behavior.
- Run cargo fmt, cargo test, SAT_STATS_JSON=on cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, ci_solver11_fast.
- Run repeated interleaved overhead confirmation on at least feistel_b64_k57_r18 and random_v285_s2.
- Record before/after medians, means, search counters, and proof setting in the bead comment.

How this serves the larger project goal:
Solver 11 is supposed to become a Kissat-class optimization branch. Section 0 instrumentation is useful only if it does not distort performance baselines. This bead restores a trustworthy baseline before later Phase 1 changes are judged.

title: Make SAT_CHRONO=on default for kissat-feature configs
description:
Task class: default policy change. Promotes chronological backtracking to default based on third-pass evidence.

Background: Solver 11 has SAT_CHRONO opt-in (default OFF). Kissat has chrono=1 default ON (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/options.h:21).

Evidence from log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md, Phase 1 results:
- M_chrono_only is the BEST single-flag config in aggregate (1025.9s PAR-2, +19% vs A_default 862.7s)
- M_chrono_only solves ALL 10 instances (no timeouts)
- Per-instance wins under M_chrono:
  * mp1-Nb7T46: 19.4s (vs A 46.9s) — 2.4x speedup
  * Kakuro-easy-112: 134.1s (vs A 243.8s) — 1.8x speedup
  * velev-pipe-sat-1.0-b7: 42.9s (vs A 74.7s) — 1.7x speedup
- Per-instance losses under M_chrono:
  * REGRandom-K4: 206.8s (vs A 63.0s) — 3.3x regression
  * battleship: 92.7s (vs A 23.5s) — 4x regression

The +19% PAR-2 aggregate is regression by absolute number but it's the smallest regression among kissat-feature configs that solve all 10, AND it unlocks several mid-tier wins (mp1, Kakuro, velev). Plus chrono is structurally simpler (no DB / restart cadence side effects) so it composes more cleanly with other features in the future.

Proposed change: in SolverConfig::default() (config.rs:580), change chrono_backtrack from false to true. Add a SAT_CHRONO=off override to opt out.

Important caveat: chrono interacts with target-phase. The previous (second-pass) bead SAT-playground-6wg decouples target-phase from EMA — this bead is independent (chrono works without EMA). But combinations should be tested.

Implementation notes:
- One-line default change in config.rs.
- Add CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv entry: SAT_CHRONO default = on, with note about REGRandom regression
- Update FEATURES.csv to reflect SmokeSafe + promoted=default for chrono_backtrack
- May want to dynamically disable chrono on instances classified as 'random UNSAT' (depends on Gap 12 classification)

Tests:
  test_chrono_default_on_in_config
  test_chrono_off_via_env_var

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench under default config now shows chrono active (verified via JSON_STATS chrono_used > 0 counter), aggregate PAR-2 reasonably close to current A_default (within +20%), no instance regression > 4x.

Larger project role: makes solver 11 default behavior closer to kissat's. Required for many follow-up combos (S2/S3/S5/S7 in third-pass investigation all include chrono). Note: the +19% aggregate cost is real and may delay promotion until Gap 12 (classification) lets us turn chrono off selectively on REGRandom-like instances.

title: Align EMA slow window with kissat (4096 -> 100000)
description:
Task class: parameter alignment / restart calibration.

Background: Solver 11 (src/main.rs:148-149) sets EMA window constants:
  const RESTART_FAST_ALPHA: f64 = 1.0 / 32.0;     // window = 32
  const RESTART_SLOW_ALPHA: f64 = 1.0 / 4096.0;   // window = 4096

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/options.h:49-50, averages.c:13-14):
  OPTION (emafast, 33, ...)
  OPTION (emaslow, 1e5, ...)     /* slow EMA window = 100,000 */

The fast windows are roughly aligned (32 vs 33). But solver 11's slow window is 4096, kissat's is 100,000 — a 24x difference. This means solver 11's slow EMA adapts FAR more quickly to recent glue changes, making the fast/slow ratio cross the restart trigger threshold more often than it would in kissat.

Combined with Gap 1 (no trail reuse on restart) and Gap 4 (margin 1.20 vs 1.10), this is part of why solver 11's EMA restart over-fires on UNSAT-random instances even though the per-fire conditions look conservative.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 9. The interaction with kissat-ema restart trigger and lbd-tiered reducer is documented in the earlier DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, but this specific calibration mismatch was not bead-ified.

Proposed change: change RESTART_SLOW_ALPHA from 1/4096 to 1/100000, matching kissat. Make it configurable via SAT_EMA_SLOW_WINDOW so the trade-off can be tested with a parameter sweep.

Implementation notes:
- One-line constant change.
- May need to adjust restart_min_conflicts in tandem if EMA initialization takes longer (100k slow window = 100k conflicts before slow EMA stabilizes).
- Should be tested specifically with SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema enabled.

Tests:
  test_ema_slow_window_matches_kissat_after_change
  test_ema_restart_trigger_less_volatile_with_large_slow_window

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Parameter sweep on benchmarks/profiling under SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema shows restart count reduced 1.5-3x on REGRandom (currently 28k restarts on mp1 under C_lbd_ema) and trail rebuild waste decreased proportionally.

Larger project role: closes Gap 9 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Companion to the trail-reuse work (existing bead 5b2.2.35); both together should make EMA restart no worse than Luby on UNSAT instances.
notes:
Started in s11-04 after closing SAT-playground-5b2.2.58. Scope: align opt-in focused/stable Kissat EMA slow window with kissat and add SAT_EMA_SLOW_WINDOW for calibration; default/fast profile remains legacy-luby so solver11 promotion gate is not triggered.

title: Fix mark_learned_clause_recent bump semantics to match kissat (Gap 3)
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic correctness. Refines the kissat lbd-tiered port semantics to match kissat's reference behavior.

Background: solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:2255-2266 in mark_learned_clause_recent currently uses:

    let recent = self.learnt_used_recently(clause_idx).max(1);
    self.set_learnt_used_recently(clause_idx, recent);

This bumps the used_recently counter back to at least 1 when a learned clause is used as a propagation reason. By contrast, kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/learn.c:110 and src/deduce.c:18) sets used to MAX_USED on every learn or reason use:

    c->used = MAX_USED;   /* MAX_USED = 31, a 5-bit field, see clause.h:14-17 */

kissat then ages used by 1 per reduce pass (reduce.c:70-72). So a kissat clause used recently is fully protected for ~MAX_USED reductions, regardless of when it was created. Solver 11's max(used, 1) semantics protect a fresh-then-reused clause for at most 1 additional reduce pass — far less than kissat.

Evidence: deeper investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Gap 3) verified the divergence by reading kissat source line-by-line and tracing the keep rule in solver 11. Per-instance ablation showed this is one of two compounding mechanisms (with Gap 2 fixed-fraction deletion) that make D_lbd_tiered+E_lbd_ema_tiered keep the wrong subset of clauses.

Proposed change (2-part, atomic):
1. Set used = MAX_USED_RECENTLY in mark_learned_clause_recent instead of max(used, 1).
2. Consider widening MAX_USED_RECENTLY from 3 toward kissat's 31. A conservative first step is 7 or 15 (single u8 widening, no storage change). The current 3 was chosen pre-kissat-port and is too narrow.

Distinction from SAT-playground-5b2.2.51: that bead proposed reducing MAX_USED_RECENTLY 3→2 to age clauses faster, which was rejected on the 11-instance suite (log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-rejected-summary.md). That fix changes the wrong dimension. The semantic fix proposed here (bump-to-MAX on use) is independent of MAX value: it preserves recently-used clauses better regardless of MAX. Closing 5b2.2.51 in favor of this bead is reasonable once this lands.

Implementation notes:
- One-line change in mark_learned_clause_recent (src/main.rs:2255-2266) plus optional MAX_USED_RECENTLY constant widening at src/main.rs:142.
- record_current_mode_glue_use should remain on every use (separate concern; current bead 5b2.2.49 audits that path for percentile bias).
- Update tests in src/main.rs:7710-7712 (used_recently after learn) and any test using mark_learned_clause_recent (~lines 7855, 7861).

Tests:
  test_mark_recent_resets_to_max_used
  test_aged_then_reused_clause_recovers_full_protection
  test_max_used_widening_does_not_break_tier_classification

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass, profile bench with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered measurably reduces learned_clauses_final on per-instance basis OR retains them longer when reused. Per the +3% promotion rule, kept clauses should improve PAR-2 by >3% on the 10-instance profiling suite under D_lbd_tiered config.

Larger project role: closes one of four kissat-port implementation gaps identified in the 2026-05-24 deep investigation. The other three are: trail reuse on restart (existing bead 5b2.2.35), fraction-based reducer deletion (new bead to be created), and restart margin alignment (existing bead 5b2.2.41 needs new-evidence note).

title: Preserve target_phase across focused/stable restarts; reject all-mode persistence
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic bug. Root cause for the lack of differentiation between SAT_PHASE=saved and SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved / best-then-target-then-saved across recent matrices.

Background: src/main.rs:4086-4103 `perform_restart_if_pending`:

    fn perform_restart_if_pending(&mut self) -> bool {
        if !self.restart_pending { return false; }
        self.restart_pending = false;
        self.reset_target_phase();           // <-- wipes target_phase, target_assigned = 0
        if self.current_level() == 0 { return false; }
        ...
        self.maybe_rephase_on_stable_restart();
        self.backtrack(0);
        true
    }

`reset_target_phase` (src/main.rs:3848-3854) sets `target_phase.fill(UNASSIGNED)` and `target_assigned = 0`. This fires on EVERY restart (legacy-luby, kissat-ema, reluctant).

`maybe_capture_phase_prefix` (src/main.rs:3882-3903) writes into `target_phase` only when `assigned > self.target_assigned`. With Luby restarts firing every ~32-256 conflicts in the early-search regime, target_phase is reset before it accumulates a meaningful trail prefix. The next capture starts from `target_assigned = 0` and refills only the trail seen in the new (shorter) restart cycle.

Consequence: `target_phase[var]` is UNASSIGNED most of the time when `pick_branch_phase` consults it (src/main.rs:3801-3805 PhasePolicy::TargetThenSaved, src/main.rs:3815-3820 PhasePolicy::BestThenTargetThenSaved). The phase lookup falls through to `saved_or_initial_phase`, making `TargetThenSaved` behave indistinguishably from `Saved`. The `stats.phase_target_used` counter is small relative to `stats.phase_saved_used` in default-style configurations, confirming this in artifacts.

Kissat behavior for comparison:
- target_phase is reset on rephase / mode switch / specific milestones, NOT on every restart.
- target_phase accumulates the best trail prefix seen across many restart cycles within a phase block.
- best_phase is reset even less often (only on rephase).

Current SOLVER11_STATE.md text "Target phases are preserved across focused/stable mode switches and are reset only by restart handling" describes the current implementation, but the design choice that target should be wiped on every restart appears to be unintentional (no design note in the closed bead SAT-playground-5b2.2.8 [1.5] justifies it).

Goal: stop resetting target_phase on every restart. Keep the reset on:
- mode switch (focused <-> stable) - already handled separately in 5b2.2.23/24
- rephase events - already happens via `apply_rephase`
- explicit milestones if any are added later

Implementation notes:
- Remove `self.reset_target_phase();` from `perform_restart_if_pending`.
- Verify `maybe_capture_phase_prefix` already handles the "grow watermark" case correctly (it does: `if assigned > self.target_assigned`).
- Verify `reset_target_phase` is still called from the intended paths. Grep: `git grep -n reset_target_phase solver/11-kissat-port/src/`. Expected callers post-fix: mode switch handling and rephase. If nothing else calls it, the function may become dead.
- For `best_phase`, audit similarly. `capture_best_phase` only runs when `search_mode_policy == FocusedStable` OR `phase_policy == BestThenTargetThenSaved`. Confirm best_phase is not also wiped on restart.

Side question (file as follow-up if needed): `maybe_capture_phase_prefix` is called AFTER `run_post_propagation_scheduling` in the search loop (src/main.rs:5858-5863). Even after this fix, the first no-conflict iteration after a pending restart captures phase on the (now-truncated) trail. Hoisting the capture call above `run_post_propagation_scheduling` would let it record the long pre-restart trail. Consider as part of this fix OR a sibling bead.

Tests:
- test_target_phase_survives_restart (set target_phase via maybe_capture_phase_prefix, fire a restart, assert target_phase still populated)
- test_target_assigned_monotone_across_restarts
- test_target_phase_reset_on_rephase (regression: ensure rephase still clears as intended)
- test_pick_branch_phase_uses_target_after_restart
- existing phase / restart tests must continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved, both in single mode and focused-stable mode. Counters: phase_target_used, phase_best_used, phase_saved_used, phase_initial_used (after SAT-playground-5b2.2.43 lands), restarts, luby_restarts. Expected: phase_target_used materially larger relative to phase_saved_used. PAR-2: improvement on SAT-heavy and mixed classes; neutral on UNSAT-heavy.

Risk IDs: R5 (search trajectory), R6 (phase-saving invariant from 5b2.2.8). Rollback: restore reset_target_phase call in perform_restart_if_pending.
acceptance_criteria: Focused/stable target_phase is no longer wiped by perform_restart_if_pending; single-mode target policies keep restart-time target reset because all-mode persistence caused profile regressions; rephase resets target_phase to start a new phase block; regression tests cover focused/stable survival, single-mode reset, monotone focused/stable target_assigned, target branch selection after focused/stable restart, and rephase reset; cargo test, smoke checks, and 11-instance 300s profile comparison pass without status regression.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review (second pass). Likely root cause for SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved / best-then-target-then-saved failing to differentiate from SAT_PHASE=saved in past matrices, and a prerequisite for re-evaluating the phase-policy axis in SAT-playground-5b2.2.46.

Initial all-mode removal of reset_target_phase from every restart passed unit/smoke checks but regressed the target-phase 11-instance 300s profile from 9/11 PAR-2 1642.134 to 7/11 PAR-2 2614.777, with new Timetable and REGRandom K4 timeouts. Final patch preserves target_phase across restarts only when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable, keeps single-mode restart reset behavior unchanged, and resets target_phase on rephase. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo test target 14 passed; cargo test rephase 8 passed; cargo test 304 passed; default smoke 9/9; invariant smoke 9/9; SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved smoke 9/9; SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_REPHASE=on SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved smoke 9/9. Final profile: log/phase1/1.14t-target-phase-preserve-profile-before -> log/phase1/1.14t-target-phase-preserve-profile-after-focused-only, SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved SAT_STATS_JSON=on SAT_TRACE_FULL=on, 11 instances, 300s, 16GiB: 9/11 -> 9/11, PAR-2 1642.134 -> 1642.230, no status changes. Summary artifact: log/phase1/1.14t-target-phase-preserve-summary.md.

Focused/stable restarts now preserve target_phase, single-mode target policies keep restart-time reset after all-mode persistence caused profile regressions, and rephase clears target_phase for a new phase block. title: Re-run 1.16 focused/stable matrix after throughput subset (1.14r/s/u/w/aa) lands
description:

The accompanying stats (log/phase1/1.16-matrix/summary.md) show propagations/s dropped from 4,649,873 (default) to 1,222,290 (focused/VMTF guard100) — a 74% throughput regression that is not explained by search trajectory.

A 4× propagation-throughput drop is consistent with the per-call overhead the open 5b2.2.18.* throughput subtasks already identify: the accounting_mode branch in propagate_impl (1.14s), per-watcher search_ticks RMW (1.14u), per-reason LearnedMeta lookups (1.14r/1.14w), and the per-variable accounting/search_mode branch in bump_analyzed_variable_activity (1.14aa). The 1.16 matrix ran *before* any of those landed, so the comparison was 'high-overhead focused/stable' vs 'low-overhead default,' not 'equal-overhead focused/stable' vs 'equal-overhead default.'

Goal: re-run the 1.16 matrix exactly as before, after the throughput subset lands. If the focused/VMTF aggregate PAR-2 movement holds without throughput penalty, and mp1 is recovered or its loss is much smaller, the deferred verdict changes. title: Fix phase_initial_used stat mislabeling in Legacy phase policy
description:
Task class: solver-behavior bug fix in telemetry.

Background: src/main.rs:3766 in pick_branch_phase for PhasePolicy::Legacy increments self.stats.phase_initial_used += 1 and then returns self.saved_phase[var]. The phase actually returned is the saved phase (which enqueue updates on every assignment at src/main.rs:3114-3116), not the initial phase from self.initial_phase(var) / self.original_phase. The counter is therefore mislabeled.

title: [1.4a] Glucose-style blocking restart from level EMA
description:
Task class: solver-behavior / performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs already maintains restart_fast_level and restart_slow_level EMAs (fields at main.rs:961-963, updated in update_restart_ema at main.rs:3416-3417), but should_restart (main.rs:3420-3440) never reads them. The plan section 1.4 declares the fields but does not specify the consuming condition. Modern Glucose / Kissat block restarts when the recent trail/level EMA is significantly above its slow average, signalling a productive SAT prefix; suppressing the restart preserves that prefix.

title: Fix: high-LBD learned clauses get lower initial used_recently than Kissat
description:
In solver 11's learn path (~main.rs:1990), newly learned clauses are initialized with used_recently based on their tier:
  - LBD <= TIER2_MAX_GLUE (6): used_recently = 3
  - LBD > 6 (tier3): used_recently = 1

Kissat always sets c->used = MAX_USED (value 31, a 5-bit field saturating at 31) at learn.c:110, regardless of the clause's glue. This gives every newly learned clause maximum initial protection from deletion regardless of quality.

The used counter is decremented during reduce_db passes. Starting high-LBD clauses at used_recently=1 instead of the maximum means they can be collected after the very next reduce_db, before they have had a chance to be used. This makes the tier3 clause retention policy more aggressive than Kissat's and may cause useful clauses to be deleted prematurely.

Implementation:
1. In the learn/add_learned_clause path, initialize used_recently to the same maximum value (e.g. 3 or whatever the u8 MAX_USED analog is) regardless of the clause's LBD tier.
2. Let the reduce_db decrement logic determine when the clause is evictable, not the initial value.
3. If desired, keep a lower initial value ONLY for clauses whose LBD exceeds a very high threshold (e.g. > 20), but align first with Kissat's uniform initialization and measure the effect.
notes: s11-01 progress 2026-05-22: Selected as next logical Phase 1 blocker after bv triage. This is the narrowest P2 search-policy bug before larger LBD-tier/reduce scheduling work: newly learned high-LBD clauses currently start with less deletion protection than Kissat's MAX_USED initialization, which can bias later reduce_db experiments and prematurely delete clauses before they have a chance to prove useful. Implementation plan: align initial used_recently for every learned clause with the solver's MAX_USED_RECENTLY analog, update focused tests/docs, run cargo tests, smoke/invariant checks, and profile benchmark.
close_reason: Implemented uniform learned-clause initial used_recently retention. initialize_learnt_lbd now sets every newly learned clause to MAX_USED_RECENTLY regardless of LBD tier, matching Kissat's maximum initial learned-clause used counter semantics while leaving tier classification, reduce-DB aging, and reason-use marking unchanged. title: Fix: kissat_update_scores not called when entering stable mode
description:
Kissat calls kissat_update_scores (bump.c:114-120) when switching TO stable mode in mode.c:183. This refreshes the VSIDS heap so that variable scores accumulated during focused mode are correctly reflected in the heap order before stable mode begins making decisions.

Solver 11's maybe_switch_search_mode() (~main.rs:3340) handles mode transitions but only resets the VMTF search pointer for the focused-to-stable direction. It does NOT rebuild or reschedule the VSIDS heap. As a result, the stable-mode heap may have stale ordering at mode entry, causing early stable-mode decisions to be suboptimal.

Implementation:
1. Identify the stable mode entry branch in maybe_switch_search_mode.
2. After setting the mode to stable, call a heap-rescore or reschedule function equivalent to kissat_update_scores: iterate over unassigned variables and re-insert them into the VSIDS heap with their current bump scores.
3. Alternatively, mark the heap as dirty and lazily rebuild on the next pick_branch_lit call in stable mode.

This is a correctness/quality issue for the focused -> stable transition, not just a micro-optimization. Kissat reference: mode.c:183, bump.c:114-120.
notes: s11-01 progress 2026-05-22: Selected after bd ready and bv triage/plan. Ignored container epics and chose the ready P2 focused/stable behavior blocker. Rationale: stable-mode decisions depend on the VSIDS heap, while focused-mode VMTF can let VSIDS scores change without guaranteeing a clean stable-entry heap order. Fixing this narrow mode-transition issue should precede larger reduce_db schedule, dynamic tier, and search-tick mode-gating work. Plan: add a Kissat-style stable-entry heap refresh/rebuild, cover stale-heap behavior with a unit test, update current-state docs, run focused mode tests, full unit/smoke/invariant checks, an advanced focused/VMTF smoke, and the default profile benchmark.
close_reason: Implemented stable-entry VSIDS heap refresh for focused/stable mode. maybe_switch_search_mode now rebuilds the branch heap from current variable activities whenever the new mode is Stable, matching the role of Kissat's update_scores before stable decisions resume. Focused-entry behavior remains unchanged: LBD EMA averages reset and VMTF search cursor resets when entering Focused. Added test_mode_switch_to_stable_refreshes_vsids_heap_scores to simulate stale heap ordering after focused-mode score changes and verify stable mode picks the refreshed top variable. Updated README, SOLVER11_STATE, and plan text. Fresh-eyes review covered mode-switch reachability, VMTF pick path, VSIDS pick path, heap rebuild filtering, backtrack reinsertion, default-mode reachability, and docs; no additional implementation bugs found. title: Fix: mode switching uses conflict count for both modes; stable should gate on search ticks
description:
Kissat uses two different limits for mode switching (mode.c):
- Focused → stable: CONFLICTS >= limits.mode.conflicts, where the interval is nlogpow(count/2, 4) * modeint (nlogpow is n * 4th-power of log2(n)). This grows super-linearly with mode count.
- Stable → focused: search_ticks >= limits.mode.ticks, where delta_ticks is the tick count from the previous stable phase. Stable mode is sized by actual propagation work, not conflict count.

Solver 11 (maybe_switch_search_mode, main.rs:3329) uses conflicts for both modes with sqrt(mode_switches + 1) * scale * init_conflicts scaling. This:
1. Does not use search ticks for the stable-mode gate (missing propagation-work accounting).
2. Uses sqrt scaling instead of Kissat's nlogpow(count, 4) for the focused-mode gate. nlogpow grows much faster, giving focused mode longer intervals as search progresses.
3. Does not call any equivalent of kissat_init_averages when switching modes (mode.c calls this to reset all averages on every switch, not just the EMA restart values handled by bead 5b2.2.24).

Required changes:
1. Add search_ticks counter incremented at each literal visit in propagation (in the watcher scan inner loop). Ticks are the mechanism Kissat uses to measure inprocessing and mode work.
2. Use search_ticks as the stable-mode gate instead of conflicts.
3. Change focused-mode interval formula to nlogpow(focused_mode_count, 4) * base_interval.
4. On every mode switch, reset all mode-sensitive averages (not just EMA restart values).

Note: add SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on config flag as an opt-in until validated, so the change does not silently alter default behavior before benchmarking.
notes:
Implemented 2026-05-22 in solver/11-kissat-port. Added SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on as an opt-in config/feature flag. In tick mode, propagation records search_ticks for binary implication edges, watcher visits, and long-clause replacement literal visits during normal search only; temporary assumptions do not tick. Focused/stable mode switching now matches the Kissat shape behind the flag: focused mode still switches by conflicts, focused intervals use Kissat nlogpown(count, 4) * mode_init_conflicts with log10(count + 9), stable mode switches by search_ticks using the previous mode's tick delta, and all restart EMAs (LBD and level, fast and slow) reset on every tick-mode mode switch. title: Fix: LBD-tiered reduce_db trigger uses literal/clause budget, not SQRT-scaled conflict limit
description:
Kissat fires reduce_db when CONFLICTS >= limits.reduce.conflicts, then schedules the NEXT reduce at current_conflicts + SQRT(reductions) * base_interval (reduce.c:193: UPDATE_CONFLICT_LIMIT(reduce, reductions, SQRT, false)). The initial interval is ~1000 conflicts, growing as sqrt(k) after k reductions.

Solver 11's LBD-tiered path uses two triggers (should_reduce_db, main.rs:3924):
  live_learned_clause_count - trail.len() >= reduce_db_limit   (clause-count based)
  OR learned_literals > learned_lit_budget                       (literal-count based)

The literal-count budget also scales with reductions (refresh_learned_lit_budgets uses sqrt(reduction_count)), but the clause-count trigger fires first and does not scale properly with the LBD-tiered policy. The clause-count path is a MiniSat-legacy artifact that interacts poorly with the tiered policy: as tier3 clauses accumulate, live_learned_clause_count grows faster than the trail, firing reduce every 5-10 conflicts.

Fix: for ReducePolicy::LbdTiered, replace the primary trigger with a conflict-count limit that starts at reduceinit (e.g. 1000) and grows as SQRT(reduce_db_calls) * base_interval. Keep the hard literal limit as an emergency overflow guard only. Add SAT_REDUCE_INIT config key for the base interval.

This eliminates the cascading GC that produces 12,025 reductions in 60s on mp1 (1 per 6 conflicts). Kissat gets 26 reductions for the same instance on a SQRT-scaled schedule.
notes: Completion note 2026-05-22: Implemented LBD-tiered reduce_db scheduling as a conflict-count schedule, not legacy learned-clause/literal pressure. For SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered, reduce_db_limit now means the next absolute conflict count. Defaults: first reduction at 1000 conflicts; reschedule after each reduction to current_conflicts + sqrt(reduce_db_calls) * SAT_REDUCE_DB_INTERVAL/default 1000. SAT_REDUCE_DB_INIT and SAT_REDUCE_DB_INTERVAL remain the existing config knobs; no duplicate SAT_REDUCE_INIT was added. Legacy reduction behavior keeps its learned-clause-count trigger and MiniSat-style budget adjustment. The normal learned_lit_budget is now only the deletion target inside a scheduled LBD-tiered reduce, not a trigger. The hard learned-literal guard remains an emergency trigger but now scales as max(64 * learned_lit_budget, 64 * original_literals), refreshed after initial clause load and after preprocessing, so it does not fire continuously on large formulas. Fresh-eyes review caught and fixed an initial bug where hard budget was too low: mp1 direct trace initially still did 10809 reductions by 590k conflicts; after the final guard fix the same 60s trace ended at 580k conflicts with 91 reductions, matching the intended SQRT schedule shape. title: Fix: LBD-tiered reduction uses static tier thresholds; needs per-mode histogram
description:
Solver 11 uses hardcoded TIER1_MAX_GLUE=2 and TIER2_MAX_GLUE=6 (main.rs:68-69). Kissat computes tier limits dynamically from a per-mode glue usage histogram (tiers.c). The histogram tracks how often clauses at each glue level are accessed since the last retier; tier1 is set to cover the top 50% of used clauses by frequency (TIER1RELATIVE=0.5) and tier2 covers the top 90% (TIER2RELATIVE=0.9, options.h:152-154).

With avg_lbd=50+ in focused/stable mode, static tier1=2 and tier2=6 means virtually all learned clauses are tier3, which triggers constant GC. Dynamic tiers would push the thresholds up to match the actual distribution (e.g., tier1~25, tier2~70 on mp1), keeping the best-used clauses protected.

Second gap: Kissat decrements c->used on EVERY reduce pass for every redundant clause (reduce.c:71: 'if (used) c->used = used - 1'), including those NOT being deleted. This slowly ages clauses off their tier protection. Solver 11 never decrements used; clauses with used_recently=true stay protected indefinitely.

Required changes:
1. Add per-mode glue usage histogram: stats.focused_glue_used[glue] and stats.stable_glue_used[glue] incremented at deduce time (in add_analyzed_clause_from_slice / mark_learned_clause_recent).
2. Implement compute_tier_limits() that reads the histogram for current mode and computes 50th/90th percentile thresholds. Call it at the start of reduce_db_lbd_tiered().
3. In the reduce pass, decrement used counter for all scanned redundant clauses (not just those being deleted).

Evidence: mp1 focused/VMTF 60s run, log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf: reductions=12025, avg_lbd=50.4. Kissat on same instance: reductions=26. The 462x difference in GC frequency is primarily caused by static tier thresholds at 2/6 vs a dynamic ~25/70.

If reduce_db_lbd_tiered (src/main.rs:4562) still sorts by raw f64 activity for tie-breaking, the planned integer-key invariant has not landed yet. Cheap to verify alongside the per-mode-histogram work and worth a sub-fix so 5b2.2.31 lands in the planned shape.
Audit note 2026-05-22 (sub-fix from fresh-eyes pass): also evaluate the TIER1_MAX_GLUE constant. solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:68 sets TIER1_MAX_GLUE=2 statically. Combined with the recent fix (commit 6849f82) that initializes used_recently=MAX for every tier, the tier1/tier3 protection asymmetry is carried entirely by size/used_recently keys in ReduceCand. Modern Kissat moves the tier1 boundary upward during stable mode rather than holding it at 2. When implementing per-mode histograms here, also try a small sweep: tier1 in {2, 3} x mode in {focused, stable} on search-core + discriminating, with per-mode learned-LBD histograms attached to the writeup. Record rejected variants with counters so the next loop does not retry blindly.

title: Fix: EMA restart state not reset when entering focused mode
description:
In maybe_switch_search_mode() (main.rs:3329), the fast/slow LBD EMA values (restart_fast_lbd, restart_slow_lbd) are not reset when switching modes. Kissat resets EMA windows on mode transitions so each mode phase starts with a clean restart calibration.

When entering focused mode from a stable phase that had high average LBD (e.g., 50+), the slow EMA is calibrated to stable-mode statistics. The EMA-based restart then fires at the wrong rate in the new focused phase because the baseline is wrong.

Evidence from mp1 focused/VMTF run (log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf): glucose_restarts=329, reluctant_restarts=5497. The tiny number of glucose restarts (329) despite many focused-mode decisions suggests the EMA is calibrated to a high-LBD baseline from stable mode and slow to trigger in focused mode, while reluctant restarts (stable mode) dominate.

Fix: when switching to focused mode, call restart_fast_lbd.reset() and restart_slow_lbd.reset() (set initialized=false, value=0.0) so focused mode starts its EMA from scratch. Do not reset on switch to stable because stable uses reluctant restarts, not EMA. Add a test confirming EMA state is clean after a focused-mode switch.

Reference: Kissat src/restart.c — resetema() called from mode.c switchmode() on entering focused mode.

title: Fix: target_phase incorrectly cleared on focused/stable mode switches
description:
In maybe_switch_search_mode() (main.rs:3348), reset_target_phase() is called on every mode switch. Kissat does NOT do this — target phase accumulates continuously across mode switches and is only cleared on restarts (perform_restart_if_pending, main.rs:3714).

Clearing target_phase on mode switch discards all phase information accumulated during the preceding focused epoch whenever the solver transitions to stable mode. This degrades SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and best-then-target-then-saved policies, which are the default for focused/stable mode.

Evidence: the 1.12a retest (log/1.12a/summary.md) shows focused/VMTF on mp1 with phase_save_target=707,779 (many target captures), but the solver fails to use them effectively because they get cleared on every mode switch (mode_switches=10 in 60s).

Fix: remove reset_target_phase() from maybe_switch_search_mode(). Verify target_phase is still cleared on restarts only. Add a test that confirms target_phase is preserved across a mode switch.

Reference: Kissat src/phases.c — targetresetphases() is only called from restart.c, never from mode.c.

title: [0.13] Repair trace and diagnostic config flag parsing
description:
Background:
While debugging the Section 0 overhead, an integration bug surfaced: solver 11's CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv and allowed_env_vars list include SAT_TRACE_PROOF, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS_DETAILS, and SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL, but SolverConfig::apply_env_overrides currently parses SAT_TRACE_FULL and SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS while skipping the individual trace flags. A direct run with SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL=1000000000 produced no solver 11 search summary, while solver 10 emitted the expected final search counters.

Goal and intent:
Make the trace/diagnostic flags documented by Section 0 actually work. These flags are needed to debug overhead, compare search trajectories, and support later optimization work without ad hoc code edits.

Implementation guidance:
- Parse SAT_TRACE_PROOF, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS_DETAILS, and SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL in SolverConfig::apply_env_overrides.
- Ensure replay override behavior remains consistent with the schema and allowed_env_vars.
- Add tests that construct env maps and assert the corresponding SolverConfig fields are set.
- Add a small integration-style test or documented command proving SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL causes solver 11 to emit final search counters.
- Ensure SAT_TRACE_FULL still implies preprocess and detail tracing as intended.

Constraints and considerations:
- This is not the main performance fix, but it enables reliable debugging and overhead gates.
- Avoid increasing default runtime overhead; trace flags must remain disabled by default.
- Keep schema, README, validator, and generated artifacts consistent.

Testing expectations:
- cargo test must cover env parsing.
- A direct smoke command with SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL set should show a final `c search done ...` line.
- Run ci_solver11_fast after the fix.

How this serves the larger project goal:
Future Phase 1 and Phase 2 work needs trustworthy diagnostics. Trace flags that appear in the config contract but do not execute create false confidence and make regression analysis slower.
