## 0.3 Single configuration object, feature flags, profiles, and validation

### Goal

Avoid scattered `std::env::var` calls in hot paths. All feature selection should go through one parsed config object, with reproducible profile defaults and strict validation for invalid combinations.

### Implementation

Add:

```rust
struct SolverConfig {
    // Reproducibility / profile selection.
    profile: SolverProfile,
    proof_policy: ProofPolicy,
    feature_statuses: Vec<FeatureStatus>,
    config_dump: bool,
    config_out: Option<PathBuf>,
    config_replay: Option<PathBuf>,
    config_replay_allow_overrides: bool,
    strict_config: bool,
    run_label: Option<String>,

    // Output / diagnostics.
    stats_json: bool,
    trace_full: bool,
    check_invariants: bool,
    deterministic_seed: u64,

    // Internal limits.
    conflict_limit: Option<u64>,
    propagation_limit: Option<u64>,
    tick_limit: Option<u64>,
    wall_limit_sec: Option<f64>,
    rss_limit_mb: Option<u64>,
    learned_lit_limit: Option<u64>,
    binary_clause_limit: Option<u64>,
    extension_bytes_limit: Option<u64>,
    proof_bytes_limit: Option<u64>,

    // Phase 1 search.
    use_lbd: bool,
    update_reason_lbd: bool,
    restart_policy: RestartPolicy,
    reduce_policy: ReducePolicy,
    phase_policy: PhasePolicy,
    search_mode_policy: SearchModePolicy,
    chrono_backtrack: bool,
    binary_fast_path: bool,
    clause_min_mode: ClauseMinMode,
    vmtf: bool,
    rephase: bool,

    // Phase 1 search tuning limits. These fields are listed here so references in this plan are explicit.
    // A task may not use one until it also adds parser, CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv, dump, replay, README/internal docs, and config_hash coverage.
    minimize_depth_limit: u32,
    chrono_max_delta: usize,
    mode_init_conflicts: u64,
    mode_interval_scale: f64,
    rephase_init_conflicts: u64,

    // Solver-10 compatibility and existing preprocessing controls.
    simplification: bool,
    bve: bool,
    full_bsr: bool,

    // Phase 2 simplification.
    inprocess: bool,
    vivify: bool,
    probe: bool,
    hbr: bool,
    transitive: bool,
    forward_subsume: bool,
    gate_extract: bool,
    gate_bve: bool,
    rcheck: bool,

    // Phase 2 pass budgets. A task may not reference one until it also adds parser, CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv, dump, replay, README/internal docs, and config_hash coverage.
    inprocess_interval_conflicts: u64,
    inprocess_max_rounds: u64,
    vivify_ticks_budget: u64,
    vivify_max_clause_len: usize,
    probe_ticks_budget: u64,
    eliminate_ticks_budget: u64,
    transitive_max_depth: u32,
    transitive_ticks_per_source: u64,
    transitive_max_removed_per_round: u64,
    rcheck_ticks_budget: u64,
}
```

Enums:

```rust
enum SolverProfile {
    Baseline,       // solver-10-equivalent: Safe search × Off preprocess
    Default,        // Validated Phase 1 search × Conservative preprocess
    Fast,           // Strong Phase 1 search × GateAware preprocess (target after Phase 2)
    Experimental,   // any combination of validated and unvalidated features
}

struct ProfileAxes {
    search: SearchAxis,        // Safe | Validated | Strong
    preprocess: PreprocessAxis, // Off | Conservative | GateAware
}

// Legacy profile name mapping (kept only for cross-reference with older log
// artifacts; new code must use the SolverProfile + ProfileAxes pair):
//   search-conservative  -> Default, search=Validated, preprocess=Off
//   search-strong        -> Default, search=Strong,    preprocess=Off
//   inprocess-conservative -> Default, search=Validated, preprocess=Conservative
//   inprocess-gate-aware -> Fast,    search=Strong,    preprocess=GateAware

enum ProofPolicy { Off, Drat, Lrat }

enum FeatureMaturity {
    ParkingLot,
    Experimental,
    SmokeSafe,
    OracleSafe,
    ProofValidated,
    DiscriminatingValidated,
    FullSetValidated,
}

struct FeatureStatus {
    name: &'static str,
    enabled: bool,
    maturity: FeatureMaturity,
    proof_validated: bool,
    model_validated: bool,
    full_set_validated: bool,
    validation_artifact: Option<PathBuf>,
}

enum RestartPolicy { LegacyLuby, KissatEma, Reluctant }
// MiniSat-style restart removed: it is never used or benchmarked by the Phase 1 candidate matrix
// (legacy-luby vs kissat-ema vs reluctant). If a task later motivates it, reintroduce in a focused experiment.

enum ReducePolicy { LegacyActivity, Activity, LbdTiered }

enum PhasePolicy { Legacy, Saved, TargetThenSaved, BestThenTargetThenSaved }
// `Negative` (always-false) is a degenerate case of Saved with uninitialized phase; not exposed.
// `Kissat` was an alias for TargetThenSaved; removed to keep one canonical name per behavior.

enum SearchModePolicy { Single, FocusedStable }
enum ClauseMinMode { Off, Basic, RecursiveLimited, InBlockShrink }
```

Environment variables:

Legacy compatibility variables:

```text
SAT_SIMPLIFICATION=on/off   # maps to existing solver-10 simplification default controls
SAT_BVE=on/off              # maps to existing preprocessing BVE enablement
SAT_FULL_BSR=on/off         # maps to existing full-BSR behavior
```

Compatibility rules:

```text
- legacy variables are parsed only in config.rs
- legacy variables are converted into explicit SolverConfig fields before solving starts
- legacy variables are included in config_hash and SAT_CONFIG_DUMP
- no legacy std::env::var call may remain in search, propagation, simplification, or proof hot paths
- if a legacy variable conflicts with a new explicit SAT_* flag, SAT_STRICT_CONFIG=on rejects the run
- SAT_ELIMINATE_INPROCESS is not accepted as a legacy alias; use SAT_INPROCESS plus explicit BVE flags
```

Config validation:

```text
- fail fast on unknown `SAT_*` variables when SAT_STRICT_CONFIG=on
- fail fast on invalid enum values
- normalize profile defaults before explicit per-flag overrides
- when SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY is set, load the effective config from that file
- by default, SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY rejects env overrides other than:
    * SAT_CONFIG_OUT
    * SAT_RUN_LABEL
    * SAT_STATS_JSON
    * SAT_TRACE_FULL
    * SAT_LIMIT_WALL_SEC
    * SAT_LIMIT_RSS_MB
- allow arbitrary replay overrides only with SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=on, and record `replay_overridden=true` plus the override list in JSON_STATS
- when SAT_CONFIG_OUT is set, write the effective config and config_hash before parsing CNF
- replay files must include schema_version, solver version, profile, proof policy, seed, limits, every config field, all feature flags, and per-feature maturity records
- any task that introduces a config field must add:
    * SolverConfig field
    * env var parser row
    * CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv row
    * SAT_CONFIG_DUMP output
    * replay serialization/deserialization
    * README or hidden/internal documentation status
    * config_hash coverage
- reject contradictory combinations unless explicitly marked experimental
- print effective config when SAT_CONFIG_DUMP=on
- include config_hash, profile, proof policy, and per-feature maturity summary in JSON stats
```

Invalid combinations to reject by default:

```text
- SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered with SAT_USE_LBD=off
- SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema with SAT_USE_LBD=off
- SAT_VMTF=on with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=single
- SAT_HBR=on with SAT_PROBE=off
- SAT_GATE_BVE=on with SAT_GATE_EXTRACT=off
- SAT_PHASE=target, SAT_PHASE=best, SAT_PHASE=negative, and SAT_PHASE=kissat are invalid aliases; use explicit target-then-saved or best-then-target-then-saved
- SAT_RESTART=minisat is no longer accepted; use legacy-luby, kissat-ema, or reluctant
```

Named profile intent (4 named profiles, composed from two axes):

```text
baseline (search=Safe, preprocess=Off):
  - solver-10-equivalent: no Phase 1/2 features enabled
  - kept indefinitely for A/B comparison and the "I want predictable behavior" use case

default (search=Validated, preprocess=Conservative):
  - search axis: every Phase 1 feature that passed smoke + oracle + proof + discriminating + regression-guards
  - preprocess axis: vivification + probing only (no gate-aware BVE, no HBR)
  - this is what `sat-solver` runs with no flags
  - subsumes the previous "search-conservative" and "inprocess-conservative" intents

fast (search=Strong, preprocess=GateAware):
  - search axis: default plus VMTF, rephase, recursive-limited minimization, target+best phase
  - preprocess axis: default plus HBR, gate extraction, gate-aware BVE, transitive reduction
  - target profile after Phase 2 completes
  - subsumes the previous "search-strong" and "inprocess-gate-aware" intents

experimental:
  - any combination of validated and unvalidated features
  - never used for promotion acceptance unless explicitly stated
```

Composition rule:

```text
- SAT_PROFILE=fast implies fast.search AND fast.preprocess axes.
- SAT_SEARCH_AXIS / SAT_PREPROCESS_AXIS may override the composed default.
- For example, `SAT_PROFILE=fast SAT_PREPROCESS_AXIS=conservative` is permitted via explicit axes;
  it is not a named profile and so is reported with profile=experimental in JSON_STATS but
  records the override pair.
- A run with axes not matching any named profile reports the explicit axis tuple.
```

Parking-lot flags:

```text
Do not add SAT_WALK, SAT_SWEEP, SAT_ELS, or SAT_BCE to SolverConfig until the corresponding Appendix A feature is explicitly unparked by milestone triage.
Treat those names as the parking-lot denylist: they may appear in PLAN.md only as forbidden or future-after-unpark flags, not as active config variables.
If unparked, add them in the same task that adds tests, maturity ledger entries, CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv rows, FEATURES.csv rows, and profile rules.
```

Promotion sequence:

```text
1. promote feature to experimental
2. promote into the `default` profile's search and/or preprocess axis after discriminating + regression-guards
3. mark feature ProofValidated only after proof-on validation
4. promote into `fast` only after `default` shows a stable win and the feature earns its preprocess/search axis seat
5. promote to a baseline-candidate replay artifact only after end-of-phase full-set validation
6. promote baseline-candidate to baseline only after the default-profile hardening gate
```

Candidate replay rule:

```text
- candidate runs use SAT_PROFILE=experimental until promotion
- promoted profiles (baseline/default/fast) are generated from validated SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY files, not hand-copied env snippets
- every candidate config must include SAT_PROOF, SAT_SEED, SAT_CONFIG_OUT, and concrete values for every feature flag in scope
- axis-override runs (SAT_SEARCH_AXIS / SAT_PREPROCESS_AXIS) record the explicit axis pair in JSON_STATS so promotion comparison is unambiguous
```

Default-profile hardening gate:

```text
- README examples run successfully through config replay
- tools/ci_solver11_fast.sh passes
- tools/ci_solver11_matrix.sh passes
- tools/ci_solver11_proof_model.sh passes
- full-set proof-off and proof-on scorecards are both attached
- regression-guards have no lost solved instances unless accepted in milestone triage
- SAT model validation passes on SAT-heavy smoke-plus and discriminating SAT instances
- UNSAT proof verification passes on proof-heavy UNSAT set
- memory limits and extension/proof budgets have no unexplained UNKNOWN spikes
- compare_bench.py report includes no unchecked UNSAT proofs and no SAT model-check failures
- FEATURES.csv rows for every baseline-enabled feature have validation artifacts
```

Per-feature maturity ledger:

```text
solver/11-kissat-port/FEATURES.md:
  - one row per feature flag
  - current maturity
  - proof/model validation state
  - last validation artifact path
  - promoted profiles that enable it
  - risk IDs
```

Machine-readable maturity ledger:

```text
solver/11-kissat-port/FEATURES.csv:
  - feature_flag
  - config_field
  - maturity
  - proof_validated
  - model_validated
  - full_set_validated
  - promoted_profiles
  - validation_artifact
  - risk_ids
  - last_changed_task
```

Single source of truth: the `SolverConfig` struct is annotated with a `#[config_field(...)]` attribute (proc macro or `build.rs` code generation) that captures: env variable, allowed values, per-profile defaults, conflicts/requires constraints, is_feature_flag, is_legacy_alias, introduced_task, and short description. Similarly, `enum SolverFeature` variants carry `#[feature(maturity=..., proof_validated=..., ...)]` attributes.

At build time, codegen emits:

```text
target/generated/CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv        # for tooling and CI
target/generated/config_env_parser.rs     # env parsing, no hand-written std::env::var
target/generated/config_dump.rs           # SAT_CONFIG_DUMP output
target/generated/config_replay.rs         # serialize/deserialize replay files
target/generated/README_config_table.md   # included into README via a one-line include
target/generated/FEATURES.csv             # derived from SolverFeature variants
```

The generated `CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv` and `FEATURES.csv` retain the same columns documented elsewhere in this plan (env_var, config_field, type, allowed_values, per-profile defaults, is_feature_flag, is_limit, is_legacy_alias, conflicts_with, requires, introduced_task, documented_in_readme; and for FEATURES.csv: feature_flag, config_field, maturity, proof_validated, model_validated, full_set_validated, promoted_profiles, validation_artifact, risk_ids, last_changed_task).

Rules:

```text
- SolverConfig (with #[config_field]) and SolverFeature (with #[feature]) are the only hand-edited config/feature artifacts.
- Adding a config field requires only: one struct field, one #[config_field(...)] attribute, one CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv golden-diff review.
- Generated CSVs are checked into the tree and refreshed by `cargo run -p solver11-codegen`. A CI step regenerates and fails on drift.
- FEATURES.md is human-facing commentary and may be generated or manually maintained.
- SAT_CONFIG_DUMP includes the maturity row for every enabled feature.
- A promoted profile that enables a feature missing a `validation_artifact` attribute fails `cargo build` at codegen time, not at CI.
```

```text
All new features default off until validated.
Defaults are changed one at a time only after milestone/profile promotion.
Feature maturity is tracked per feature, separately from performance profile selection.
No feature may enter the `default` or `fast` profile (or any non-baseline named axis combination) unless FEATURES.csv names the validation artifact.
```

## 0.1 Architecture boundary and ownership map

### Goal

Prevent solver 11 from becoming a larger `main.rs` monolith while preserving solver 10 behavior.

### Additional architecture rule: capability-based mutation (introduced incrementally)

Module extraction is not enough. New subsystems must receive the narrowest capability object that can perform their job, not unrestricted `&mut Solver`. However, capability types are introduced **incrementally**, when the first task that needs the seam is implemented. Pre-declaring six capability wrappers during the fork stage forces a large refactor before any algorithmic change requires it.

Until a task introduces the first capability seam, the rule is simpler:

```text
- No `pub fn` in a new pass module (1.x or 2.x) takes unrestricted `&mut Solver` if the function does not need it.
- The first task that introduces a capability type (likely 1.0a, with `TemporaryAssumptionCtx`) sets the pattern: a private newtype wrapping `&mut Solver`, exposing only the subset of methods needed by callers.
- Subsequent passes follow the same pattern, but capabilities are added in the task that first needs them, not pre-declared in 0.1.
- The "no unrestricted &mut Solver" rule applies only to new pass modules; existing `Solver::*` methods inherited from solver-10 are exempt until a task explicitly refactors them.
- capability structs expose methods only; their fields remain private.
- pass modules may not store capability objects beyond a single call frame.
- no public method on a capability may return `&mut Solver`.
- `validate_solver11_plan.py` scans new `src/*` pass modules for `pub fn .*&mut Solver`.
- SOLVER11_STATE.md includes an `unrestricted_mut_solver_exceptions` table with expiry task IDs (the table starts empty and is populated as capabilities are added).
- After 2.1a, all destructive formula edits must go through whatever capability `InprocessCtx`-equivalent exists at that point (the 2.1a task defines the exact type).
```

Expected capability roll-out order (informative, not normative):

```text
1.0a  introduces TemporaryAssumptionCtx
1.6   introduces a propagation-level capability if binary fast path needs it
2.0   introduces InprocessCtx
2.1   introduces ProofCtx (proof finalization/temp lifecycle)
2.1a  introduces ModelCtx (extension-entry append)
2.6+  occurrence-list capability when BVE scheduling refactor needs it
```

Each of the above is a normal task that adds tests, an SOLVER11_STATE.md row, and a migration of the call sites it touches. None of them are required before task 1.0.

### Implementation

Before algorithmic changes, create module boundaries in two stages.

Stage A is mandatory before Phase 1 and should be small:

```text
src/config.rs       SolverConfig, parsing, validation, profile/default selection
src/stats.rs        counters, timers, JSON/trace output
src/lit.rs          literal/variable encoding helpers
src/limits.rs       conflict/propagation/tick/wall-clock limit checks
src/output.rs       status/model/proof-path contract and temp-proof lifecycle
src/check.rs        invariant checks and original-CNF model verification
```

Stage B is incremental and should happen only when a task needs the boundary:

```text
src/arena.rs        clause arena, ClauseRef, clause header/meta helpers
src/trail.rs        assignment, decision levels, reasons, trail frames
src/watch.rs        long watchers, binary implications, propagation contracts
src/proof.rs        DRAT/proof buffering and proof event API
src/model.rs        extension-stack replay and original-CNF assignment repair
src/branch.rs       heap/VMTF/rephase phase-selection machinery
src/search.rs       CDCL search loop, restart/reduce/mode policy glue
src/simp.rs         existing BVE/BSR/occurrence machinery
src/inprocess.rs    scheduler and pass orchestration only
```

Extraction rules:

```text
- each extraction patch is behavior-preserving
- no new feature flag changes behavior during extraction
- no algorithmic tuning in extraction patches
- every module exposes narrow methods rather than public fields
- every module documents the invariants it owns
- do not move an entire subsystem merely to satisfy the map; move code when the next task needs the seam
- add façade methods first, then move internals later
- every extraction patch must pass a solver-10-vs-solver-11 status comparison on smoke-plus
```

Minimum ownership contracts:

```text
Trail owns:
  - assignment values
  - decision levels
  - trail frames
  - reason references

Watch owns:
  - long watcher mutation
  - binary implication adjacency
  - propagation conflict representation

Arena owns:
  - clause layout
  - learned/original metadata
  - GC reference rewriting entry points
  - debug generation checks for ClauseRef and ClauseHandle

Proof owns:
  - DRAT add/delete output
  - proof temp-file lifecycle
  - proof counters

Model owns:
  - original-CNF model check
  - extension-stack replay

Capability ownership (applies once each capability is introduced; see roll-out order above):
  - `PropagationCtx`, when introduced, owns no allocation-heavy buffers and must not allocate in steady-state propagation.
  - `InprocessCtx`, when introduced, is the only capability allowed to commit FormulaEditTxn after 2.1a.
  - `ProofCtx`, when introduced, is the only capability allowed to finalize or rename proof files.
  - `ModelCtx`, when introduced, is the only capability allowed to append destructive-edit extension entries.
  - Until each capability lands, the equivalent rule applies to the existing `Solver::*` methods that perform that role, and the introducing task migrates the call sites in the same patch.
```

### Tests

```bash
cd solver/11-kissat-port
cargo test
cd ../..
bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
```

### Acceptance

```text
- behavior matches baseline before and after extraction
- no feature default changes
- no new public cross-module mutable access to trail/watch/arena/proof internals
- SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on catches stale ClauseRef/BinaryClauseId use after a forced GC/rebuild test
```

Debug handle tests:

```text
test_debug_clause_ref_generation_rejects_deleted_slot
test_gc_rewrite_visitor_updates_all_registered_clause_refs
test_binary_clause_id_generation_rejects_deleted_binary_in_debug
```

## 0.0 Fork to a new solver directory

### Goal

Create an identity copy of solver 10 that can be A/B tested against the unchanged baseline.

### Implementation

```bash
cp -R solver/10-bve-preprocess solver/11-kissat-port
```

Update `solver/11-kissat-port/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "sat-solver-11-kissat-port"

[[bin]]
name = "sat-solver"
path = "src/main.rs"
```

Update any local `build.sh` / `run.sh` references while preserving the binary contract:

```text
run.sh <cnf-path> <out-dir>
```

Keep release profile settings identical to solver 10. Do not relax optimization settings.

Add:

```bash
tools/run_solver11_baseline.sh
tools/status_compare.py
tools/validate_solver_result.py
```

`tools/validate_solver_result.py` validates one solver output directory:

```text
inputs:
  - --cnf <path>
  - --out-dir <path>
  - --expected-status SAT|UNSAT|UNKNOWN|PARSE_ERROR|any
  - --proof-policy off|drat
  - --require-json-stats on|off

checks:
  - status file exists and matches documented schema
  - SAT model satisfies the original CNF
  - UNSAT proof exists and verifies when proof policy is drat
  - UNKNOWN has no finalized proof and no model
  - ParseError has no model or finalized proof
  - JSON_STATS required fields exist when requested
```

`tools/status_compare.py` is a minimal pre-0.5 helper: it reads two existing `results.csv` files, compares instance/status pairs, reports solved-count deltas if the columns exist, and has no dependency on `benchmarks/iteration/baseline.csv` or `tools/compare_bench.py`.

Script contents:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd solver/11-kissat-port
cargo test

cargo build --release

cd ../..
bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
mkdir -p log/baseline-lock

bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/profiling solver/10-bve-preprocess \
  --log-dir log/baseline-lock/solver10

bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port \
  --log-dir log/baseline-lock/solver11

python3 tools/status_compare.py \
  --before log/baseline-lock/solver10/results.csv \
  --after log/baseline-lock/solver11/results.csv \
  > solver/11-kissat-port/BASELINE_LOCK.raw.txt

{
  echo "solver10_dir=solver/10-bve-preprocess"
  echo "solver11_dir=solver/11-kissat-port"
  echo "date_utc=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  echo "rustc=$(rustc --version 2>/dev/null || true)"
  echo "cargo=$(cargo --version 2>/dev/null || true)"
```

title: Implement random decisions for diversification in focused mode
description:
Task class: search diversification. Implements kissat's per-conflict-interval random decision injection.

Background: Kissat's pick_branch_lit equivalent (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/decide.c:86-153) injects random decisions during focused-mode search:
- Default randec=1, randecfocused=1, randecstable=0 (random only in focused)
- Initial interval randecinit=500 conflicts
- After interval, runs a sequence of randeclength=10 random decisions (length grows logarithmically)

Solver 11's pick_branch_lit (src/main.rs:3934) always picks from VSIDS heap or VMTF queue. No random injection.

Evidence from log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 7: Indirect evidence — solver 11 + VMTF beats kissat on mp1 (1.5s vs 8.7s), but loses to kissat on battleship (0.9s vs 0.18s) where lucky + random_decisions explain most of the gap.

Random decisions matter most on instances where:
- The optimal search trajectory contains a 'jump' that no greedy heuristic would pick
- VSIDS/VMTF builds biased preference for variables not actually on the SAT path
- The instance has many viable SAT models reachable from different decision orders

Proposed change: add SAT_RANDEC=on flag (default OFF initially) that injects random decisions per kissat's schedule:
1. Track conflicts_since_last_randec
2. When >= randec_interval, start a 'random sequence' of randec_length decisions
3. During sequence: pick a random unassigned variable instead of heap/VMTF top
4. After sequence completes, resume normal picking
5. Schedule the next random_interval to grow logarithmically (kissat uses kissat_logn)

Implementation notes:
- Need a seeded RNG (already have DEFAULT_DETERMINISTIC_SEED in solver 11)
- Pick from active unassigned variables; respect VSIDS/VMTF for backup
- Add stats counters: random_decisions, random_sequences

Tests:
  test_random_decisions_triggered_after_interval
  test_random_decisions_eventually_yield_normal_branching
  test_random_decisions_deterministic_with_seed

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Parameter sweep on benchmarks/profiling shows neutral aggregate (within 5%) for default OFF, and at least one instance (likely battleship or a similar SAT-trivial) improves when SAT_RANDEC=on enabled.

Larger project role: closes Gap 7 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Modest expected impact alone, but composes with Gap 5 (VMTF) for SAT-leaning instances and may close the kissat gap on battleship-style trivial-SAT instances.

title: Decouple SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved from EMA restart in default kissat configurations
description:
Task class: configuration / default-bundle policy. Prevents future kissat-feature combinations from including SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved when SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema is active.

Background: deeper investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 3 sweep table) tested three configurations that bundle target-phase with EMA restart or with lbd-tiered:
- H5 (C_lbd_ema + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)
- H6 (D_lbd_tiered + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)
- H7 (E_lbd_ema_tiered + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)

All three regress 6s299b685_Iter30 by 7-8× (146s / 124s / 145s vs A_default 17s). The HWMCC hardware-verification instance solves in 3,764 conflicts under baseline / B / C / D, but jumps to 7,000-32,000 conflicts under any target-phase variant. The target-phase heuristic (saves an assignment between restarts) gives the wrong polarity on this instance type, causing wasted re-search.

Other Iter30 regressions confirming the bundle is the issue:
- F_full_kissat (E + target-phase + chrono): Iter30 127s
- G_focused_stable (uses best-then-target-then-saved): Iter30 94s

By contrast, configs that omit target-phase keep Iter30 in 16-18s range:
- C_lbd_ema: 18.2s
- D_lbd_tiered: 17.1s
- E_lbd_ema_tiered: 18.1s
- H1 (C + block_margin): 16.3s
- H4 (E + block_margin): 17.4s

Distinction from SAT-playground-5b2.2.45: that bead documents how SAT_PHASE behaves under SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable mode. This bead is about not BUNDLING target-phase with EMA restart in default kissat-feature configs (independent of focused-stable mode).

Implementation notes:
- Today SAT_PHASE is opt-in (default Legacy). The bundling issue arises when a kissat-style 'default kissat profile' is constructed in config.rs and includes target-phase + kissat-ema together.
- Either: (a) keep SAT_PHASE=legacy as the kissat-feature default when EMA is on, and require explicit user opt-in for target-phase; or (b) detect HWMCC-style instances and skip target-phase saving for them; or (c) document this combination in CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv as 'do not combine with kissat-ema unless instance is known to benefit from saved-phase' and never make it default.
- The simplest minimum-disruption path is (a): never include SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved or best-then-target-then-saved in the same default profile as SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema.

Tests:
  test_default_kissat_profile_does_not_combine_target_phase_with_ema
  test_target_phase_remains_opt_in_when_ema_active

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Verify in source review (config.rs, profile defaults) that no compound profile includes both phase=target-then-saved and restart=kissat-ema by default. Add a CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv note documenting the rationale.

Larger project role: prevents the F_full_kissat-style 7-8× Iter30 regression from appearing in future default bundles. This is a guardrail, not an algorithmic change. Related to 5b2.2.45 (which documents phase override semantics inside focused-stable mode); this bead is about default-bundle hygiene more broadly.

title: Eliminate per-call Vec<bool> allocation in reduce_db_lbd_tiered
description:
Task class: solver-behavior performance bug. Companion to SAT-playground-5b2.2.47 (LBD allocation) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.11 (rebuild_reason_pinset scratch reuse).

Background: src/main.rs:5033-5085 `reduce_db_lbd_tiered` allocates a `Vec<bool>` of size `self.arena.len()` on every reduce-DB call:

    let mut delete_clause = vec![false; self.arena.len()];

The arena grows monotonically with original + learned + (later GC'd) clause slots. On medium-suite instances we see arena sizes in the millions of slots; on competition instances this can be tens of millions. Each LBD-tiered reduce currently pays:

1. `vec![false; arena.len()]` allocation + zero-fill.
2. Walk of `candidates` (post-sort) to mark `delete_clause[cand.clause_idx] = true`.
3. Walk of `learned_clause_ids` (size O(live learned)) to gate eviction by `delete_clause[clause_idx]`.
4. Free.

Step 1 touches the entire arena footprint (a multi-MB memset) even though only the small set of marked candidates needs to be looked up. The current schedule fires every sqrt(reduce_db_calls)*interval conflicts, so on long runs the cumulative cost is significant.

This bead violates plan section 2 invariant "propagation, conflict analysis, decision selection, and reduce-db candidate scans do not allocate in steady state" (called out in 5b2.2.18.11 description). 5b2.2.18.11 covers `rebuild_reason_pinset` but not this site.

Goal: replace the per-call `Vec<bool>` with a sparse marker. Two reasonable shapes:

Option 1 (preferred): keep candidates already sorted by eviction priority, then walk them once to mark using a u64 generation stamp on a Solver scratch vector. The scratch is allocated once at solver construction, sized to `arena.capacity()`, and grown only on arena reallocation. Reset is O(1) (bump generation), like the existing `lbd_stamp` pattern.

    self.reduce_delete_gen = self.reduce_delete_gen.wrapping_add(1).max(1);
    if self.reduce_delete_gen == 0 { self.reduce_delete_mark.fill(0); self.reduce_delete_gen = 1; }
    // mark survivors during the candidate walk:
    for cand in candidates { ... self.reduce_delete_mark[cand.clause_idx] = self.reduce_delete_gen; ... }
    // then walk learned_clause_ids and check membership by gen:
    if self.reduce_delete_mark[clause_idx] == self.reduce_delete_gen { ... evict ... }

Option 2: sort `candidates` by `clause_idx` after the LBD-priority sort, then do a merge-join with `learned_clause_ids` (also sorted by clause_idx normally) to avoid the membership marker entirely. More invasive.

Implementation notes:
- The scratch vector needs to be grown to `arena.len()` when arena grows beyond previous capacity. Cheapest place to check is at the start of `reduce_db_lbd_tiered`.
- Make sure `garbage_collect` either invalidates the scratch (zero-fill or bump generation) since clause indices reloc.
- Same scratch could be reused by `reduce_db_legacy_activity` if that path is changed similarly, but legacy uses in-place sort + filter and does not allocate this Vec, so it's out of scope for this bead.

Tests:
- test_reduce_db_lbd_tiered_no_per_call_allocation (tracking allocator, force several reduces in succession)
- test_reduce_delete_marker_handles_arena_growth (extend arena between reduces)
- test_reduce_delete_marker_generation_wraparound (bump generation past u64::MAX trigger via wrapping_add)
- existing reduce-DB-lbd-tiered tests must pass unchanged (learned_kept_tier1/2/3 counters, evicted clauses)

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered. Counters: reduce_db_calls, learned_collected, GC counters. perf stat on a run with many reduce_db_calls (REGRandom K4 with capped timeout, or a synthetic deep run) — expect the allocator pressure proxy and dTLB miss count to drop. Expected PAR-2: neutral-to-improved (no semantic change; pure overhead removal).

Risk IDs: R10 (allocation invariant), R3 (learned-clause correctness). Rollback: restore the per-call Vec<bool>.
acceptance_criteria: reduce_db_lbd_tiered no longer allocates a Vec<bool> sized to arena.len() per call; tracking-allocator test confirms zero per-call allocation; cargo test, smoke, and lbd-tiered profile benchmark all pass without regression.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review (second pass). Companion to SAT-playground-5b2.2.47 (compute_lbd) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.11 (rebuild_reason_pinset). Together these three sites are the dominant per-reduce-DB allocation cost.

Rationale: .47 removed the LBD clause Vec allocation and passed same-mode profile before/after, but the lbd-tiered reason-update mode still times out mp1 versus default-off. This bead targets the next ready allocation hotspot in the same reduce/LBD throughput group.

Tests cover marker arena growth, generation wraparound, and zero allocations across repeated no-candidate reduce passes when the marker is reused. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo test 299/299; default smoke 9/9; invariant smoke 9/9; SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered smoke 9/9; same with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_PROP_REASONS=on smoke 9/9. title: Document SAT_PHASE override behavior in focused-stable mode
description:
Task class: documentation / configuration contract.

Background: src/main.rs:3526-3540 effective_phase_policy silently overrides the user-supplied SAT_PHASE value when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable is on:

    Focused mode: Legacy or Saved → Saved
                  TargetThenSaved or BestThenTargetThenSaved → TargetThenSaved
    Stable mode: anything → BestThenTargetThenSaved

So a user setting SAT_PHASE=legacy SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable does not get the Legacy phase policy in focused mode; they silently get Saved. A user setting SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved in focused mode gets TargetThenSaved (best is only used in stable mode).

This override is reasonable Kissat-style behavior (focused mode favors target-phase guidance, stable mode favors best-phase consolidation) but it is documented nowhere user-facing:
- README.md at solver/11-kissat-port/README.md lists SAT_PHASE values without saying focused-stable overrides them.
- FEATURES.md / FEATURES.csv do not mention the override.
- CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv lists conflicts/requirements but does not record this overlay.

Goal: add a one-paragraph note in README.md under SAT_PHASE explaining the override matrix, plus a row in FEATURES.md for SAT_SEARCH_MODE noting it overlays SAT_PHASE values. Optionally add a SAT_CONFIG_DUMP output that records the effective policy alongside the user-supplied policy so artifact triage shows both.

Implementation notes:
- README change is small and orthogonal to code.
- If the dump shape changes, src/config.rs::dump and the replay file format need a schema bump or backward-compatible field; consider a follow-up rather than tying it to this bead.

Tests:
- a config-schema test asserting the documented override table matches effective_phase_policy is helpful but optional.

Benchmark gate: none. Documentation only.

Risk IDs: none. Rollback: revert the README/FEATURES edits.
acceptance_criteria: solver/11-kissat-port/README.md describes the SAT_PHASE override matrix when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable is on. FEATURES.md notes the overlay. cargo test and smoke pass (no code change).

title: Gate mark_binary_clause_used per-prop writes behind SAT_STATS_HOT
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:1937-1942 mark_binary_clause_used:

    fn mark_binary_clause_used(&mut self, binary_id: BinaryClauseId) {
        if let Some(binary) = self.binary_clauses.get_mut(binary_id.0 as usize) {
            binary.used_count = binary.used_count.saturating_add(1);
            binary.last_used_conflict = self.stats.conflicts;
        }
    }

This runs on every binary propagation in the fast path (propagate_binary_implications at src/main.rs:3171, 3175) and on every binary reason walked in conflict analysis (mark_binary_literals_for_analysis at src/main.rs:5218). It performs two writes per binary prop unconditionally — used_count saturating-add and last_used_conflict store — into BinaryClause records that may not be L1-resident. With SAT_BINARY_FAST=on on binary-heavy formulas this is per-propagation overhead with no diagnostic switch.

Search this codebase for consumers of binary.used_count and binary.last_used_conflict: they feed diagnostic/trace output only (no production decision relies on them). They are reported in SAT_TRACE_FULL output as binary clause-usage histograms.

Goal: gate the writes behind self.hot_stats (the SAT_STATS_HOT flag already used to gate watch_scans / binary_props etc. in propagate_impl). Default off → no writes → no per-prop cost. SAT_STATS_HOT=on still emits the histograms for profiling runs.

Implementation notes:
- Pass HOT_STATS down through propagate_binary_implications and the binary-reason analysis path; mark_binary_clause_used::<HOT_STATS>().
- Alternatively: take a normal_search_accounting + hot_stats pair and skip the writes when either is false. Keep mark_binary_clause_used on conflict-side calls (mark_binary_literals_for_analysis) gated the same way.
- This composes with [1.14s] (TEMP const generic for propagate accounting) — both touch the same per-binary-prop call site.

Tests:
- test_mark_binary_clause_used_no_writes_when_hot_stats_off
- test_mark_binary_clause_used_writes_when_hot_stats_on
- existing binary-fast-path tests must continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_BINARY_FAST=on, default hot_stats=off. perf stat: stores per second around propagate_binary_implications. Expected: lower store rate, lower L1 dcache writes per binary prop. PAR-2 effect probably small but non-zero on binary-heavy instances (Feistel, mp1).

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path writes), R12 (telemetry coverage). Rollback: revert to unconditional writes.
acceptance_criteria: With SAT_BINARY_FAST=on and SAT_STATS_HOT=off, used_count and last_used_conflict remain unchanged across binary propagations (covered by new test). With SAT_STATS_HOT=on the writes still happen. cargo test and smoke pass.
notes: Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. Pairs naturally with [1.14s] / [1.14u]; bundle if the propagate refactor lands first.

title: Avoid full O(V) heap rebuild on every focused→stable mode switch
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:2737-2739 refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores calls rebuild_branch_queue (src/main.rs:2723-2735) on every focused→stable transition. rebuild_branch_queue clears branch_heap and branch_pos, re-scans 1..self.assignment.len() to push every unassigned decision variable, then sifts down. This is O(V) work and is paid on every mode switch.

In focused mode the heap is still maintained: bump_variable_activity (src/main.rs:3363-3377) sift-ups on every analyzed variable, and heap_reinsert_unassigned_decision_var (src/main.rs:2697) reinserts on every backtrack. So the heap is *already correct* on entry to refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores in the usual case — the rebuild is defensive against possible activity inversions during focused-mode bumping. But because heap_sift_up runs after every bump in focused mode, the only invariant the rebuild fixes is that previously VMTF-picked vars (which were heap_remove_assigned_top'd via pick_vmtf_branch_var → branch_heap_remove) need reinserting. Those vars are already reinserted by heap_reinsert_unassigned_decision_var on backtrack.

Goal: skip the full rebuild on transitions that do not need it. Two acceptable shapes:
- (preferred) drop refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores entirely and replace with a no-op or assertion that the heap is well-formed. Add a debug_assert that heap_invariant_holds.
- (conservative) keep the rebuild but gate it: only run when VMTF was active during the prior focused mode (self.vmtf_branching_active() was true). Skip otherwise.

Implementation notes:
- maybe_switch_search_mode at src/main.rs:3633 calls refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores when transitioning to Stable; that is the only caller besides tests.
- Profile a focused-stable run with SAT_VMTF=on to confirm the heap is consistent at the transition point. heap_invariant_holds tests can be added to src/main.rs tests.
- If kept, the rebuild can also be made incremental: walk vmtf_queue to find vars that were popped from the heap but not reinserted, and reinsert only those.

Tests:
- test_branch_heap_consistent_after_focused_stable_transition_with_vmtf
- test_branch_heap_consistent_after_focused_stable_transition_without_vmtf
- existing mode-switch tests continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_VMTF=on. Counters: mode_switches, time around maybe_switch_search_mode (add a timer if not present). Expected: lower wall time on instances with many mode switches, no change to conflict counts / search trajectory.

Risk IDs: R5 (search trajectory if heap is left inconsistent). Rollback: restore unconditional rebuild_branch_queue.
acceptance_criteria: The full O(V) rebuild is gated or removed for the common case. heap invariant remains after every mode switch (covered by new debug_assert + tests). No PAR-2 regression on focused-stable+VMTF runs. cargo test and smoke pass.
notes: Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. Not previously captured under 5b2.2.18.* throughput subtasks.

title: Remove dead should_restart function (eliminates build warning)

Option (a) is the minimal change and matches current production behavior. title: [1.14ab] Cache clause header and hoist loop-invariant config flags in conflict-analysis hot path
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: A sweep of the conflict-analysis hot path found three small but related cleanups that share the same fix family (cache loop-invariant or repeated-load values once). Bundled into one bead because each individual item is below the typical bench noise band; together they may be measurable, and they all touch the same functions.

Item A: mark_reason_literals_for_analysis reloads clause_header twice (src/main.rs:5210-5217)
    if LBD_META && self.update_reason_lbd && clause_idx < self.arena.len()
        && self.clause_is_learnt(clause_idx)
        && !self.clause_is_deleted(clause_idx)
    { ... }
clause_is_learnt and clause_is_deleted both call clause_header(clause_idx) (= self.arena[clause_idx]). Fix: cache once.
    let header = self.clause_header(clause_idx);
    if clause_header_learnt(header) && clause_header_mark(header) != CLAUSE_DELETED_MARK { ... }

Item B: clause_activity / set_clause_activity reload the clause header per call (src/main.rs:1828-1843)
Each helper calls self.clause_len(clause_idx) which loads self.arena[clause_idx]. bump_clause_activity in src/main.rs:3239-3258 does both a read and a write, so two header loads for one update. Fix: introduce a fused with_clause_activity_mut(clause_idx, |act| ...) (or two helpers that accept a precomputed extra_idx) so the header is loaded once. Composes cleanly with [1.14d] (5b2.2.18.4 / s11-1-14d) if f32 activity lands: the fused helper still benefits.

Item C: Loop-invariant runtime flags checked per literal/reason in conflict analysis
- mark_clause_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5137-5138) checks self.use_resolved_conflict_analysis once per literal walked.
- mark_binary_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5175-5176) checks the same per literal.
- mark_reason_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5207) checks self.reduce_policy == ReducePolicy::LbdTiered once per reason walked.
All three are config-time invariants. Fix options:
  (a) Hoist into local bools at function entry and pass into the inner loop.
  (b) Extend the existing LBD_META const generic with a USE_RESOLVED and a LBD_TIERED const generic so monomorphization removes the branches entirely. Mirrors the HOT_STATS / MODE_TICKS pattern already used elsewhere in the propagate path.

Implementation notes:
- Items A and B are local refactors; tackle first.
- Item C requires touching the call sites in analyze_conflict_to_scratch / analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl. The existing LBD_META const generic already shows the pattern; add USE_RESOLVED and LBD_TIERED alongside it.
- Verify the existing tests for resolved-conflict-analysis and LBD-tiered reduction continue to pass on every variant of the const generic combinations.
- Do all three under one PR so the conflict-analysis hot path is touched once rather than three times.

Tests:
- Existing conflict-analysis / LBD / resolved-conflict tests must pass unchanged.
- test_const_generic_specializations_match_baseline (synthetic sweep over all combinations of LBD_META / USE_RESOLVED / LBD_TIERED).
- test_clause_activity_fused_helper_matches_split_helpers.

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered (and one run with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on to exercise the Item A path). perf stat for branches / branch-misses / L1-dcache-load-misses around the conflict-analysis call on wide-UIP instances. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement; no behavior change.

Skip rule: if profiling after the rest of the 5b2.2.18.* block shows conflict analysis is no longer a hot path, this bead may be rejected with a note in log/phase1/triage.md.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout). Rollback: revert to current per-call header reads and per-literal flag checks.

title: [1.14aa] Hoist accounting_mode / search_mode branches out of bump_analyzed_variable_activity
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: bump_analyzed_variable_activity in src/main.rs:3393-3402 contains loop-invariant branches per iteration:

    for &var in &bumped_vars {
        if !self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() && self.search_mode == SearchMode::Focused {
            self.vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var(var);
        }
        self.bump_variable_activity(var);
    }

Neither self.accounting_mode nor self.search_mode changes during the loop. The compiler may LICM-hoist these via inlining, but the indirect call to vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var (which itself rereads self.vmtf_queue.as_mut()) blocks aggressive optimization across the call boundary.

Goal: hoist the two checks. Two clean options:
  (a) Read both bools once before the loop into locals; branch outside the loop into either a VMTF-stamping or non-stamping variant. Costs code duplication but removes the branches.
  (b) Const-genericize a small finalize_analyzed_variables<const IS_FOCUSED_NORMAL: bool>(...) so monomorphization compiles the branch out. Mirrors the HOT_STATS / MODE_TICKS pattern already used elsewhere.

Implementation notes:
- Pair with [1.14z] (5b2.2.18.11): once the clear-seen pass fuses into bump_analyzed_variable_activity, the combined fused/hoisted function is the per-conflict finalize routine.
- Verify vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var still validates its own preconditions (var > 0, decision_var, not eliminated) — those checks need to remain because they vary per var.

Tests:
- test_finalize_analyzed_variables_focused_normal_stamps_vmtf
- test_finalize_analyzed_variables_stable_does_not_stamp_vmtf
- test_finalize_analyzed_variables_temporary_does_not_stamp_vmtf
- existing VMTF / activity-bump tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_VMTF=on (the only configuration where the branch was non-trivial). perf stat for branches and branch-misses around the conflict-analysis call. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement; no behavior change.

Risk IDs: R10. Rollback: revert to runtime branch.

title: [1.14z] Fuse scratch_bumped_vars clear-seen and activity-bump into one pass
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: After UIP construction, analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl in src/main.rs:5304-5308 walks scratch_bumped_vars to clear scratch_seen and scratch_resolved:

    for &var in &self.scratch_bumped_vars {
        self.scratch_seen[var] = 0;
        self.scratch_resolved[var] = 0;
    }

Then immediately afterwards, the search loop calls bump_analyzed_variable_activity (src/main.rs:3393-3402) which walks scratch_bumped_vars AGAIN to do VMTF stamping and activity bumping. Two full passes over the same vector per conflict, on conflict-analysis-frequent code.

Goal: fuse. Combine the clear-seen / clear-resolved / vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var / bump_variable_activity work into a single iteration. The four operations do not conflict (they update independent fields keyed by var).

Implementation notes:
- The cleanest path is to delete the trailing clear-loop in analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl and move that work into bump_analyzed_variable_activity (rename it if desired, e.g. finalize_analyzed_variables).
- The fused function still needs the std::mem::take dance (or a by-index iteration; see also gap below) to call &mut self methods like bump_variable_activity.
- Pair with [1.14aa] (hoisted branches in bump_analyzed_variable_activity, see SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.12) so the per-iteration body is simultaneously minimal and branch-free for the common case.
- Verify the order: clear-seen must happen before any path that re-reads scratch_seen for the same var, but bump_variable_activity does not touch scratch_seen. Order is unconstrained between the four ops.

Tests:
- test_fused_finalize_clears_scratch_seen
- test_fused_finalize_clears_scratch_resolved
- test_fused_finalize_bumps_activity_in_same_call
- test_fused_finalize_stamps_vmtf_when_focused
- existing conflict-analysis / activity-bump tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on. Counters: conflict-analysis time if measurable; perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around the conflict-analysis call on wide-UIP instances (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500). Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement on conflict-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout). Rollback: split back into two passes.

title: [1.14y] Reuse scratch buffers in rebuild_reason_pinset to satisfy reduce-db no-alloc invariant
notes: Audit note 2026-05-23 (sixth-pass review): in addition to the per-call Vec allocation, the iteration source is wrong. `for &reason in &self.reason` walks the full per-variable reason array (length num_vars + 1), even though only ASSIGNED variables can have a non-None reason. The right iteration source is `self.trail` (which already enumerates exactly the assigned variables). On a 100k-var formula with a 5k-deep trail mid-search, the current code touches ~95k null entries per reduce-DB / GC call. When this bead lands, switch the iteration to walk trail literals and map them to var indices via `lit.unsigned_abs() as usize`. Verify with: the resulting pinned_clauses / pinned_binaries sets must be set-equivalent to the current behavior under cargo test.

title: [1.14w] Fuse LearnedMeta lookups and glue histogram in conflict-analysis hot path
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: LearnedMeta access in src/main.rs goes through a two-step learned_id_by_clause[clause_idx] -> learned_meta[id] lookup, but the conflict-analysis hot path performs this pair multiple times per learned-clause reason:

- mark_learned_clause_recent (src/main.rs:2127-2138), called per learned-clause reason during the UIP walk, calls THREE separate helpers (learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, set_learnt_used_recently) — each doing its own learned_id_for_clause + meta-index. Six array accesses per reason walked.
- maybe_improve_lbd (src/main.rs:2064-2077), enabled by SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on, does FOUR-FIVE lookups per improvement: learnt_lbd, set_learnt_lbd, classify_learnt_clause (which calls learnt_lbd again and set_learnt_tier).
- initialize_learnt_lbd (src/main.rs:2050-2056) does FIVE lookups per new learned clause.
- record_current_mode_glue_use (src/main.rs:2148, reached from mark_learned_clause_recent) hits the per-mode glue histogram with a resize check + saturating_add per reason walked — another cache line touched per call.

For UIP walks touching 30+ reasons, the redundant indirections are ~150-200 per conflict, on the hottest path the solver has.

Goal: refactor so each caller obtains LearnedId ONCE (via try_learned_id_for_clause) and operates on &mut self.learned_meta[id.0] directly. Provide a fused mark_learned_reason_used(id) helper that combines: read lbd, max(used_recently, 1), write used_recently, record glue. Also batch the histogram update — accumulate per-conflict glue contributions in a small local vec (or fixed array sized to typical LBD range, e.g. [0; 32]) during the UIP walk, then commit to focused_glue_histogram / stable_glue_histogram once at conflict completion.

Implementation notes:
- Pass a LearnedId (Option<LearnedId>) into mark_reason_literals_for_analysis when the reason is a clause; reuse the LearnedId for downstream helpers.
- maybe_improve_lbd should take LearnedId too and inline its own classify path so the second learnt_lbd lookup disappears.
- initialize_learnt_lbd: capture LearnedId in allocate_learned_id, pass it to set_learnt_lbd, classify_learnt_clause, set_learnt_used_recently in a single batch.
- The local glue-histogram buffer should be a Solver scratch field reset per conflict (no per-conflict allocation).
- Keep public helpers (learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, etc.) for non-hot callers; only the conflict-analysis path changes.

Tests:
- test_mark_learned_reason_used_matches_split_helpers_on_random_inputs
- test_fused_lbd_improvement_matches_split_helpers
- test_glue_histogram_batched_matches_per_reason_histogram
- existing learned-clause / LBD / reduce-DB tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on, both with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on and off. Counters: lbd_improved, learned_used_recently_writes (add if absent), conflict-analysis time if measurable. perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around conflict analysis on a wide-UIP instance (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500). Expected: lower L1 misses per conflict; small but consistent PAR-2 improvement on conflict-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout), R3 (LBD/learned-clause correctness).
notes:
Audit note 2026-05-22 (fifth-pass review): after 5b2.2.31 closed, record_current_mode_glue_use in src/main.rs:2160-2174 now performs TWO histogram increments per call — one into focused_glue_recent/stable_glue_recent (the tier-limit driver) and one into stats.focused_glue_used/stats.stable_glue_used (the cumulative reporting histogram). Each increment is a Self::increment_glue_histogram call with its own resize check + saturating_add, touching different cache lines. Combined with the per-reason call site in mark_learned_clause_recent, this is 4 read-modify-writes per learned reason walked in conflict analysis.

The batching rewrite in this bead therefore has a stronger motivation than the original description suggested: accumulate per-conflict glue contributions in a small Solver scratch buffer (e.g. [u32; 64] sized to expected LBD range), then commit to BOTH the recent and cumulative histograms once at conflict completion. That collapses 4N hot writes into 4 final writes per conflict for N learned reasons.

If the conflict has any glue exceeding the scratch buffer cap, fall back to direct writes for those (rare, e.g. LBD>64).
Audit note 2026-05-22 (sequencing): bead 5b2.2.29 [1.14h] may move maybe_improve_lbd from conflict analysis to propagation. Run 5b2.2.29 BEFORE this bead so the lookup-fusion targets the final call site, not the conflict-analysis site that 1.14h may decommission.

title: [1.14v] Eliminate learned_clause_ids clone in bump_clause_activity rescale
[1.14u] Batch search_ticks accumulation in propagation hot loop
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: record_search_ticks at src/main.rs:2987-2992 does a read-modify-write on self.stats.search_ticks per call. It is invoked per watch scan in propagate_impl (main.rs:3101), per inner-clause literal scanned (main.rs:3191), and per binary edge probed (main.rs:3048). The MODE_TICKS const generic correctly compiles the body out when false, but in focused-stable mode (MODE_TICKS=true — its actual reason for existing, see mode_switch_at_ticks use at main.rs:3423), every scan is a single RMW on a shared cache line in self.stats.

For propagation-heavy instances doing 10^8 + scans, this is 10^8 RMWs against one cache line; even when the line is L1-resident, that is a non-trivial fraction of propagation cost. Kissat handles this with batched ticks: increment a local counter inside the inner loop, flush once at function exit.

Goal: rewrite propagate_impl / propagate_binary_implications to accumulate ticks in a local u64 declared at function entry; flush to self.stats.search_ticks at every function return point (conflict / no-conflict / early return). Keep the existing semantics under MODE_TICKS=false (no-op). Preserve correctness around mode_switch_at_ticks — the flushed counter must be visible to maybe_switch_search_mode (called from the conflict path of the search loop, AFTER propagate has returned).

Implementation notes:
- A struct LocalTickAccumulator with #[inline(always)] flush(self, stats: &mut SolverStats) might be cleaner than open-coded flush at every return.
- Audit every return path in propagate_impl (there are multiple: conflict via clause unit, conflict via long-clause, conflict via binary, normal completion); each must flush before returning.
- The flush must happen even when accounting_mode.is_temporary() — but only for the normal stats path; temporary stats stay zero anyway. Match the current behavior (record_search_ticks does the is_temporary check).
- Consider whether the same batching applies to propagations counter writes (record_propagation_accounting). That is paired with bead [1.14s] (TEMP const generic) and the two could compose.

Tests:
- test_search_ticks_match_unbatched_baseline_on_smoke
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_conflict_return
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_completion_return
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_early_unit_conflict_return
- test_search_ticks_zero_in_temporary_assumption_mode
- existing focused-stable tick-based mode-switch tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable (the path that actually consumes search_ticks). perf stat for instructions/cycle and L1-dcache-load-misses around the propagate call. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement on propagation-heavy instances; no change to mode-switch behavior.

Risk IDs: R10. Rollback: revert to per-scan record_search_ticks.
notes: s11-02 evidence 2026-05-24 from SAT-playground-5b2.2.52: perf stat was attempted but blocked by host perf_event_paranoid=4, so hardware counters were unavailable. Solver stats still show tick-mode work is huge: default K4 recorded search_ticks=27.339B for 54.448M propagations; default battleship recorded 6.280B ticks for 16.547M propagations; VMTF K4 recorded 138.849B ticks for 100.634M propagations. Full-suite focused/stable tick mode remains a trajectory problem too, not only tick RMW overhead: default tick mode PAR-2=1201.538 with mp1 UNKNOWN, while focused/stable no-ticks PAR-2=2293.353 with Kakuro TIMEOUT and Velev UNKNOWN. Keep this bead as a throughput fix, but do not treat it as sufficient for default promotion without the mode-policy/default-profile fixes.

title: [1.14t] Incremental target/best phase capture (O(delta) instead of O(trail))
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: maybe_capture_phase_prefix in src/main.rs:3574-3595 detects a new deepest unconflicted prefix and calls capture_target_phase(assigned) and/or capture_best_phase(assigned) (src/main.rs:3548-3572). Both implementations iterate the entire &self.trail from index 0, even though the previous capture already wrote target_phase[var] / best_phase[var] for every variable below self.target_assigned / self.best_assigned. The prefix is monotone-growing — everything below the prior watermark is already recorded.

This function runs in the no-conflict arm of the search loop (called from main.rs:5388), so it fires once per propagation that does not conflict. On SAT-heavy / deep-prefix instances (battleship, Timetable, DLTM_twitter), the trail can be 50k - 500k+ assignments and a new max prefix is hit frequently. That makes the function O(assigned) per call when it should be O(assigned - prev_assigned).

Goal: capture only the new tail. In capture_target_phase, iterate &self.trail[self.target_assigned..assigned] before updating self.target_assigned. Same for capture_best_phase using self.best_assigned. The unassigned guard inside the loop can be kept defensively, but the slice will only contain assigned literals at capture time (they are on the trail).

Implementation notes:
- Read self.target_assigned / self.best_assigned BEFORE the iteration; the function currently writes the new watermark at the end.
- Verify trail bounds: assigned == self.trail.len() at the call site; old watermark fits in [0, assigned].
- Keep the existing inner unassigned check as a safety net under SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on, but consider eliding it on release builds (literals on the trail are always assigned).
- The same incremental optimization applies to any future variant that iterates the trail for phase work.

Tests:
- test_capture_target_phase_only_touches_new_tail (instrument with a counter or assert no writes to indices below old watermark)
- test_capture_target_phase_handles_first_capture_at_zero_watermark
- test_capture_target_phase_idempotent_when_assigned_equals_watermark
- test_capture_best_phase_only_touches_new_tail
- existing target/best-phase tests must continue to pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved, especially on deep-trail SAT-heavy instances. Counters to inspect: phase_save_target, phase_save_best, time spent in maybe_capture_phase_prefix (add a timer if not already present). Expected: lower wall time on SAT-heavy classes, no change on UNSAT-heavy.

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path layout) and the target/best-phase invariant family from 5b2.2.8. Rollback: revert to full-trail iteration.
notes: s11-02 evidence 2026-05-24 from SAT-playground-5b2.2.52: full profiling-set runs show phase capture is not just a theoretical hot path. In current default on Iter30, phase_save_target=59842 and phase_save_best=59842 with max_decision_level=61903; search time is 82.31s versus 6.78s in single/LBD, despite only 1.52x conflicts and 1.32x propagations. In VMTF Sudoku, phase_save_target=320706 and phase_save_best=320706 with max_decision_level=307093, and the row goes UNKNOWN at 295.879s. This confirms O(trail) capture can dominate focused/stable deep-prefix rows. Logs: log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-clean/stats.jsonl and log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-vmtf-clean/stats.jsonl.

title: [1.14s] Hoist accounting_mode branch out of propagation hot path via TEMP const generic
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:2976-2982 record_propagation_accounting branches on self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() for every single propagation. The propagate_impl function already const-genericizes HOT_STATS so hot-stats writes are monomorphized out; the temporary-vs-normal accounting branch is not, so every propagation pays a (predictable but non-free) branch.

Goal: introduce a parallel TEMP const generic on propagate_impl (or refactor propagate so temporary and normal mode dispatch into separate monomorphized functions). Then record_propagation_accounting becomes either temporary_stats.propagations += 1 or stats.propagations += 1 with no branch.

Implementation notes:
- propagate() chooses TEMP at the call site based on self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() once.
- propagate_binary_implications and propagate_impl already take HOT_STATS; add TEMP alongside.
- record_propagation_accounting becomes record_propagation_accounting::<TEMP>().
- VMTF stamping, restart EMA, phase saving already guard via accounting_mode checks — those checks can also accept TEMP if it helps.

Tests:
- existing propagation / temporary-assumption tests must pass unchanged
- test_temporary_assumption_propagation_uses_temporary_stats
- test_normal_propagation_uses_normal_stats

Benchmark gate: search-core. Expected counter: lower instructions/cycle for propagate; lower per-prop branch count via perf stat. PAR-2 effect likely small but non-zero on propagation-heavy instances.

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path layout). Rollback: revert to runtime branch.
notes: s11-03 2026-05-24: During SAT-playground-5b2.2.56 I tried a narrow accounting/LBD helper hoist in the propagation path. Full profiling run log/phase1/5b2.2.56-after-prop-accounting-hoist/results.csv was PAR-2 750.454 versus the accepted prop-specialized baseline 745.558 (+4.896 worse), despite some per-instance wins; reverted. Treat this as evidence that a simple local hoist is insufficient, not as closure of the broader TEMP const-generic propagation-accounting bead.

title: [1.14r] LearnedMeta hot/cold split
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:395-402 defines LearnedMeta with lbd:u16, tier:u8, used_recently:u8, removable:bool, vivified:bool, created_at_conflict:u64 — ~16+ bytes after padding per learned clause. The hot accesses (reduce-DB candidate scoring, conflict-analysis LBD update through maybe_improve_lbd, mark_learned_clause_recent) only need lbd / tier / used_recently — 4 bytes. The cold fields (removable, vivified, created_at_conflict) inflate the side table that the reduce_db_lbd_tiered scan walks O(num_learned_clauses) times per reduction.

Goal: split LearnedMeta into a packed hot table (Vec<u32> with lbd[16] | tier[8] | used_recently[8], or three separate Vec<>s) and a cold side table for removable / vivified / created_at_conflict. Reduces L1 pressure on reduce-DB scans on instances with many learned clauses (typical of UNSAT-heavy K4 / Kakuro classes).

Implementation notes:
- Keep the existing helpers (learnt_lbd, set_learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, set_learnt_used_recently, learnt_tier) so callers are unchanged.
- Internally route to the new hot table.
- created_at_conflict and the bools move to a parallel Vec keyed by LearnedId.
- Verify the cold fields are only consulted by inprocessing / triage paths, not by the search loop.

Tests:
- test_learned_meta_hot_fields_round_trip_through_helpers
- test_learned_meta_cold_fields_unchanged_during_search
- test_reduce_db_uses_hot_fields_only
- test_lbd_improvement_updates_hot_table
- existing reduce-DB and LBD tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered, especially on UNSAT-heavy instances with large learned-clause counts (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500, aaai10-planning). perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around the reduce_db_lbd_tiered call. Expected counter: lower L1 misses per reduce-DB call; possible PAR-2 improvement on UNSAT-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout), R3 (LBD/learned-clause correctness).

title: [1.14q] Shrink per-variable arrays from usize to u32
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: solver/11-kissat-port stores several per-variable arrays as Vec<usize> (8 bytes per variable on x86_64) even though their values comfortably fit in u32:
- decision_level: Vec<usize> (src/main.rs:898)
- branch_pos: Vec<usize> (src/main.rs:933)
- reason: Vec<ReasonCode> where ReasonCode = usize (src/main.rs:900 / 523)

On a 1M-variable instance these three arrays alone consume ~24MB; halving decision_level and branch_pos saves ~8MB — often the difference between L3-resident and DRAM-bound during conflict analysis. The plan cache-layout section does not call this out; easy to miss in plan-vs-code reviews.

Goal: change decision_level and branch_pos from Vec<usize> to Vec<u32>. Document a maximum-variables invariant (e.g. < 2^31). Optionally: also pack ReasonCode into u32 (1 tag bit + 31 payload bits), capping ClauseRef and BinaryClauseId at u32; this is more invasive and should be a follow-up sub-fix.

Implementation notes:
- Introduce a typed VarLevel = u32 newtype or just use u32 directly with conversion at call sites.
- compute_lbd_from_lits (uses decision_level), conflict-analysis loops, learned_clause_asserts_at_level, debug_assert_clause_asserting_after_backtrack — all read decision_level on hot paths.
- branch_pos compares with BRANCH_NOT_IN_HEAP sentinel; ensure the sentinel fits in u32 (use u32::MAX).

title: [1.14p] Reorder binary propagation: value check before deletion check
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs propagate_binary_implications (lines 2998-3035) currently checks binary_clause_is_deleted(edge.clause_id) BEFORE matching on lit_value(edge.implied). The already-TRUE branch (edge implied literal already satisfied) is the most common outcome on most binary edges in mature search; in that branch no propagation work happens. The current ordering forces the BinaryClause load for every edge probe even when the implied literal is already TRUE.

Goal: swap the ordering so lit_value(edge.implied) is consulted first; only when it is FALSE or UNASSIGNED do we consult the deletion flag. The change is a small refactor of the propagate_binary_implications inner loop.

Implementation notes:
- After this change, deleted edges that already have lit_value(implied)==TRUE will be left in the adjacency until GC; verify this is acceptable (it is — deleted binaries are tolerated until rebuild per plan section 1.6 invariants).
- Counters (binary_stale_skips) need to remain consistent: count stale skips only when we actually consult the deletion flag.
- Pair with [1.14o] for the maximum effect: with the hot/cold split, the deletion check is also cheaper.

Tests:
- test_binary_propagation_skips_true_edge_without_deletion_check
- test_binary_stale_skip_counter_only_increments_on_consulted_deletion
- test_binary_deleted_false_edge_still_yields_conflict

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_BINARY_FAST=on. Counters to inspect: binary_props, binary_stale_skips, propagations/sec. Profile with perf stat on a binary-heavy instance before/after.

Risk IDs: same propagation correctness risk as 5b2.2.9.

title: [1.14o] BinaryClause hot/cold split for binary propagation
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:113-123 defines BinaryClause with ~32 bytes after padding (clause_ref, a, b, redundant/deleted/proof_logged/origin bools, used_count, last_used_conflict). In propagate_binary_implications (src/main.rs:2998-3035), every binary edge probe does binary_clause_is_deleted(id) which loads the full record; every actual prop also calls mark_binary_clause_used(id) which WRITES used_count and last_used_conflict into the record. The plan cache-layout invariants target BinaryEdge<=8B and "propagation walks at most one cache line per binary edge in the hot path" — the indirect BinaryClause load breaks the spirit of that invariant (effectively two cache lines per edge).

Goal: split BinaryClause so the propagation hot path touches only a tight deleted-flag side structure (Vec<bool>, packed bitset, or a u8 vec indexed by BinaryClauseId), while used_count / last_used_conflict / origin / proof_logged / redundant move to a cold side table consulted only by reduce-db, triage, proof, and inprocessing paths.

Implementation notes:
- Introduce binary_deleted: Vec<u8> (or bitset) sized to binary_clauses.len(), updated alongside the existing BinaryClause.deleted flag.
- Replace binary_clause_is_deleted hot-path callers with the new structure; keep the BinaryClause record method available for cold paths.
- Pair with [1.14p] deletion-check ordering: check lit_value first, then deletion only when needed.
- Hot/cold split must preserve BinaryClauseId stability across rebuilds.

Tests:
- test_binary_deleted_table_tracks_binary_clauses_deleted_flag
- test_propagate_binary_uses_hot_deleted_table
- test_binary_clause_cold_fields_unchanged_during_propagation
- test_binary_dedup_and_proof_paths_still_observe_cold_fields

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_BINARY_FAST=on; expected propagation/sec improvement on binary-heavy classes. Confirm watch_scans, binary_props, binary_stale_skips are unchanged in value but lower in cost. Profile (perf stat) before/after for L1-dcache load count per propagation.

title: [1.14g+] OTSS on-the-fly self-subsuming resolution
description:
Task class: solver-behavior / performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: 1.14g (5b2.2.28) tracks on-the-fly subsumption (OTFS) during clause minimization. OTSS is the related but distinct Kissat-class pass: when a learned clause minimized against reason R produces a strict subset of R, replace R in place rather than only shortening the learned clause. The scratch_resolved[] tracking introduced for resolved-conflict-analysis (use_resolved_conflict_analysis in src/main.rs analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl) is the same infrastructure OTSS needs, so the marginal code cost is small once OTFS lands.

Goal: while analyzing or minimizing a conflict, detect when the in-progress learned clause is a strict subset of a participating reason clause R; if so, strengthen R in place (delete and re-add via the proof, update watchers, update reason pin sets) under the same FormulaEdit-style discipline as the rest of search. Off by default; gated by SAT_OTSS or a sub-flag of SAT_CLAUSE_MIN.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse scratch_resolved / scratch_seen state already populated by conflict analysis.
- Require live reason guarantees (do not strengthen a locked reason without replacing it).
- Emit proper DRAT add(new) before delete(old) and update the existing learned/original clause meta.
- Counter: otss_strengthened, otss_skipped_locked, otss_skipped_proof.

Tests:
- test_otss_strengthens_long_reason_when_learned_is_strict_subset
- test_otss_skips_when_reason_is_locked

- test_otss_does_not_change_assertion_level

title: [1.14n] Variable reordering pass in main search loop
description:
Kissat calls kissat_reordering() and kissat_reorder() periodically in the main search loop (search.c:210). This pass re-sorts the VMTF queue or VSIDS-based decision ordering based on accumulated activity scores, keeping the decision heuristic aligned with recent conflict history between major resets.

Solver 11 has no reordering pass. Variable activities accumulate via VSIDS bumps and VMTF stamps, but there is no periodic step that uses this accumulated information to realign the decision structures beyond the per-conflict bump.

Implementation:
1. Add a reordering counter/interval (similar to restart and reduce intervals).
2. In the main search loop, check whether a reordering pass is due.
3. For stable mode (VSIDS heap): the heap self-maintains ordering on insert/update, so a full rebuild may not be needed — investigate whether Kissat's reorder adds significant benefit beyond heap updates.
4. For focused mode (VMTF queue): reorder means stamping variables in activity order to reset the traversal priority.
5. Gate the reordering interval on a conflict or tick count and tune empirically.

Kissat reference: search.c:210, reorder.c.
notes: Third-pass investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md) tested S6_vmtf_otfs and confirmed mode-switching plus OTFS gives 8/10 solved with mp1 (2.7s), battleship (0.95s), Kakuro (60s) wins preserved. This is the most balanced kissat-feature combo and the closest analogue to kissat's reorder-augmented focused-stable cycle on the 10-instance profiling suite. Implementing reorder may further stabilize this config.

title: [1.14m] Iterating mode: skip restart/reorder overhead after unit-clause learning
description:
Kissat sets solver->iterating=true whenever a unit clause is learned during conflict analysis (learn.c:51). The main search loop checks this flag (search.c:198) and calls kissat_iterate() to handle the unit without going through the full restart/reorder path, saving scheduling overhead when only units are produced.

Solver 11 has no iterating field or equivalent path. Every conflict cycle goes through the full should_restart + maybe_switch_search_mode sequence regardless of whether the learned clause was a unit.

Implementation:
1. Add an iterating: bool field to the Solver struct.
2. In analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl (or the learn path), set self.iterating = true when the learned clause has length 1.
3. In the main search loop, after unit propagation on a learned unit, check iterating and skip the restart check and mode-switch check for that conflict cycle. Reset iterating to false after the check.

This is most visible on UNSAT instances where unit propagation at the root generates many unit clauses late in search. Kissat reference: learn.c:51, search.c:198, iterate.c.
