title: [1.14l] Bump reason-side variable activities during conflict analysis
description:
Kissat optionally expands reason chains during conflict analysis to bump activity of variables that are NOT in the 1-UIP clause but appear in the reason clauses of 1-UIP variables (analyze.c: analyze_reason_side_literals, called after building solver->clause). This is rate-limited:
- Only fires when decision_rate < bumpreasonsrate (default 10) — i.e., skip when few decisions between conflicts.
- Bounded by bumpreasonslimit (default 10x the current analyzed set size).
- Uses exponential delay (BUMP_DELAY) when the expanded set is too large.

Solver 11's bump_analyzed_variable_activity (main.rs:3254) only bumps variables that appeared directly in scratch_seen (the 1-UIP expansion). Reason-side variables beyond the 1-UIP clause receive no activity bump. This underestimates the activity of variables that repeatedly appear in reason chains without reaching the 1-UIP cut, causing the VSIDS heap to deprioritize them.

Note: this is distinct from bead SAT-playground-5b2.2.29 (LBD-based clause tier promotion). That bead is about lowering a CLAUSE's LBD; this bead is about bumping VARIABLE activities in the heap.

Implementation: after analyze_conflict_to_scratch (main.rs line ~5240), if not in temporary context and decision_rate is below threshold, iterate scratch_conflict_clause literals, expand each variable's reason chain up to a size limit, and call bump_variable_activity for any newly seen variable. Guard with SAT_BUMP_REASONS=on flag.

Stats:
  bump_reasons_attempted
  bump_reasons_vars_added
  bump_reasons_skipped_rate
  bump_reasons_skipped_limit

title: [1.14k] Warmup phase: populate saved phases before main search
description:
Kissat runs a warmup phase (warmup.c) before the main search loop. It iterates: decide (using VSIDS/VMTF order) then propagate_beyond_conflicts (ignore conflict outcomes and keep deciding). On completion, backtrack to level 0 WITHOUT updating saved phases, so the assignment reached at maximum depth is captured in saved_phase.

This populates saved_phase with a heuristically good initial assignment before any real CDCL reasoning begins, giving the first restart something meaningful to return to. It is equivalent to a single-pass local-search initialization.

Solver 11 has no warmup. The saved_phase at search start is initialized to initial_phase (negative literal polarity per MiniSat convention, main.rs:1454), which has no structural information. The warmup would make the initial saved_phase reflect the VSIDS-guided satisfying attempt, which is typically much better.

Implementation: add a warmup() method that runs decide/propagate_beyond_conflicts (propagate accepting multiple conflicts per trail position by ignoring them and continuing to assign) until all variables assigned or timeout. Call kissat_backtrack_without_updating_phases equivalent: backtrack to 0 but leave saved_phase as the assignment captured at maximum depth. Guard with SAT_WARMUP=on flag.

Note: warmup only improves SAT instances; UNSAT instances are unaffected. On instances where the VSIDS ordering happens to find a near-complete assignment quickly, this is a free win before any conflict-driven reasoning.
notes: Third-pass investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md) recommends pairing warmup with a separate lucky-assignment heuristic (new bead SAT-playground-ide). Warmup populates saved_phase via UP-completion (one-shot); lucky tries trivial all-true/all-false assignments. The two are complementary: warmup gives a heuristically good initial assignment; lucky catches instances where a trivial assignment SATs immediately. battleship-16-31-sat is likely a lucky case (kissat 0.18s vs solver 11 0.95s with VMTF) — warmup alone wouldn't catch it because the assignment must literally be all-true.

title: [1.14j] Trail reuse on restart
description:
Kissat's kissat_restart (restart.c) calls reuse_trail() before backtracking. Rather than always backtracking to level 0, it computes the longest prefix of the current trail that should be preserved:
- Stable mode: keep all levels where the decision variable's VSIDS score exceeds the next candidate's score.
- Focused mode: keep all levels where the decision variable's VMTF stamp exceeds the next VMTF candidate's stamp.
The backtrack target is the computed prefix level, not 0. Counts tracked as restarts_reused_trails and restarts_reused_levels.

Solver 11 always backtracks to level 0 on restart (perform_restart_if_pending, main.rs:3708: 'self.backtrack(0)'). On mp1 focused/VMTF mode, avg_decision_level=882, so each restart throws away ~882 levels of propagation. Trail reuse can preserve a prefix of these, especially in focused mode where VMTF stamps identify the most-recent conflict variables.

Implementation: add reuse_trail() that walks trail_limits from deepest to shallowest and returns the level where the decision variable's score (heap) or stamp (VMTF) falls below the next-candidate threshold. Call from perform_restart_if_pending before self.backtrack(level). Guard with SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL=on flag for opt-in benchmarking.

Tests:
  test_trail_reuse_stable_keeps_high_score_prefix
  test_trail_reuse_focused_keeps_high_stamp_prefix
  test_trail_reuse_does_not_reuse_at_zero

This is the central reason kissat tolerates EMA restart cadence at all; solver 11 cannot until this lands.

title: [1.14i] Focused restart interval: logn(restarts) growth
description:
Kissat's focused-mode restart scheduling grows the inter-restart interval with each restart via kissat_update_focused_restart_limit (restart.c):
  delta = restartint + (restarts > 0 ? kissat_logn(restarts) - 1 : 0)
  next_limit = CONFLICTS + delta

where kissat_logn(n) = floor(log2(n)) + 1. So after k restarts in focused mode, the minimum conflicts between restarts grows as log2(k). This prevents focused mode from restarting arbitrarily fast once many restarts have occurred — a soft throttle on EMA restarts.

Solver 11 uses a fixed restart_min_conflicts=50 (KISSAT_EMA_RESTART_MIN_CONFLICTS=50, main.rs:76). With VMTF focused mode, the solver saw 329 glucose restarts and 5,497 reluctant restarts in 60s on mp1 (log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf). The fixed threshold does not prevent early restart storms.

Change: in note_kissat_ema_conflict (main.rs:3426) and/or perform_restart_if_pending (main.rs:3708), update restart_min_conflicts after each focused-mode restart to base + logn(focused_restart_count) - 1. Add a focused_restarts counter distinct from the glucose_restarts stat, since the logn growth should apply only to focused-mode EMA restarts.

title: [1.14h] LBD bump on reason clause improvement (kissat-style promote)
description:
In Kissat, when a clause is used as a reason during propagation and its current LBD is higher than the LBD it would get at the current decision level, its LBD is updated downward (promoted to a lower tier). This keeps frequently-used reason clauses from aging into tier 3 even if they had a high initial LBD.

Currently solver 11 only bumps LBD on conflict analysis via SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS. Reason-side bumping lowers the effective LBD of the clause database over time, directly addressing the high avg_lbd=50 regime observed in focused/stable mode.

The SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS flag already exists (config field update_reason_lbd, main.rs). Check whether it is applying the update at the correct point: it should recompute LBD of a reason clause every time it is used as a reason and update the stored LBD if the new value is lower. Verify the update happens at propagation time (not just conflict analysis) and that tier re-assignment happens immediately.

If the flag is correct, this bead is a validation; if the update is only happening at conflict analysis, move it to the propagation hot path.

title: [1.14g] On-the-fly subsumption (OTFS) in clause minimization
description:
After learning a clause, check if the new clause subsumes any existing watched clause. Kissat performs OTFS (on-the-fly subsumption) during the minimize phase: for each literal in the learned clause, scan the watcher list for existing clauses that are subsumed by the new learned clause and delete them.

This reduces the database size without a full reduce_db pass and shortens effective clause lengths → lower LBD on future learned clauses. Particularly valuable in the focused mode regime where avg_lbd is currently 50+.

Implementation: after conflict analysis and minimization, iterate over literals in the final learned clause. For each literal, check watchers for a clause whose literal set is a superset of the learned clause. If found, remove the subsumed clause. Bound the scan to avoid overhead: limit to clauses of length <= learned_len + 4, skip if learned clause has > 20 literals.

This is an independent improvement from vivification (Phase 2 bead 2.3) and can be implemented within Phase 1 since it requires no formula-edit transaction layer.

Tests:
  test_otfs_removes_subsumed_watcher
  test_otfs_does_not_remove_non_subsumed
  test_otfs_proof_logs_deletion

title: [1.14f] Reduce_db minimum conflict interval guard for high-LBD regime
description:
When avg_lbd is high, LBD-tiered reduction fires constantly because all learned clauses land in tier 3. On mp1 with focused/VMTF mode: 12,025 reduce_db calls in 60s (1 per 5ms, 1 per ~6 conflicts) vs Kissat's 26 calls on the same instance. This GC overhead drops effective conflict rate from ~9,890/s (default) to ~1,220/s — an 8x slowdown.

The root fix is lower LBD via inprocessing (Phase 2), but a guard prevents the pathology while Phase 2 is not yet active.

Change: track reduce_db_last_conflicts and add a minimum conflict interval (e.g., 100 conflicts) between successive reduce_db calls. Only fire if both the conflict budget AND the minimum interval have elapsed. The interval should be tunable via SAT_REDUCE_MIN_INTERVAL config key.

Gate: do not reduce more than once per N conflicts where N >= 50 (try 100 as default). Verify on the profiling bench and search-core that this does not regress UNSAT instances that currently benefit from aggressive reduction.

Evidence: log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf JSON stats: reductions=12025, conflicts=73125 (1 reduction per 6 conflicts). Compare Kissat log for same instance: reductions=26, conflicts=87156 (1 per 3352 conflicts).

title: Implement jumpreasons binary reason chain flattening
description:
Task class: micro-optimization. Implements kissat's binary reason chain flattening.

Background: When kissat assigns a literal L via binary propagation with reason 'other', it inspects whether 'other' itself was binary-propagated. If so, it skips the intermediate level and uses other's reason directly.

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/assign.c:32-45):
  if (GET_OPTION (jumpreasons) && level && a->binary) {
    other = a->reason;  /* a is 'other's assigned record; jump to a->reason */
  }
  kissat_assign (...);

Default jumpreasons=1 (ON).

Solver 11's enqueue path stores binary reasons directly without chain flattening.

The effect: during conflict analysis, traversing binary reason chains is shorter under kissat. On binary-heavy formulas (kissat's classification.bigbig flag — > 99% binary clauses), this saves several iterations per reason in the analyze loop.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 11. Not measured directly on the profiling suite (most instances aren't bigbig), but a clear semantic feature of kissat that solver 11 doesn't have.

Proposed change: in solver 11's enqueue/assign path, when assigning a literal via binary propagation:
1. Check if the 'other' literal in the binary clause is itself binary-assigned
2. If so, look up other's reason and use that
3. Otherwise use the current binary reason

Implementation notes:
- The binary-fast path (src/main.rs:3261-3299, propagate_binary_implications) is the place to do this.
- Need to inspect ReasonRef::Binary for the 'other' literal in the binary clause.
- One extra indirection but flattens the chain.

Tests:
  test_jumpreasons_flattens_chain
  test_jumpreasons_off_keeps_direct_reasons
  test_jumpreasons_preserves_correctness_of_drat_proof

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass with SAT_USE_LBD=on smoke. Profile bench shows no regression on the 10-instance suite. On binary-heavy formulas (would need to identify candidates), conflict analysis should traverse fewer reasons.

Larger project role: closes Gap 11 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. P4 / low priority — modest expected impact unless instance set shifts to binary-heavy formulas. Implementation is small but care needed for DRAT proof correctness.

title: Align minimization depth limit with kissat (1M -> 1k)
description:
Task class: parameter alignment. Tightens solver 11's recursive minimization depth limit to match kissat's reference.

Background: Solver 11 (solver/11-kissat-port/src/config.rs:14):
  const DEFAULT_MINIMIZE_DEPTH_LIMIT: u32 = 1_000_000;

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/options.h:82):
  OPTION (minimizedepth, 1e3, 1, 1e6, 'minimization depth')

Solver 11's default depth limit is 1000x larger. In recursive clause minimization (lit_redundant in src/main.rs:1450+), this means solver 11 can descend through up to 1 million levels of reason chains before giving up. Kissat caps at 1000.

In practice, depths rarely exceed several hundred on typical instances. But on pathological learned clauses with deep reason chains (e.g. instances with chained binary clauses), solver 11 can spend significant time on a single minimize call that kissat would bound.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 10. Not directly measured as a hot path in the 10-instance suite (instances are small enough), but a clear semantic divergence that could matter on harder instances.

Proposed change: change DEFAULT_MINIMIZE_DEPTH_LIMIT from 1_000_000 to 1_000 in config.rs:14.

Implementation notes:
- One-line constant change.
- SAT_MINIMIZE_DEPTH_LIMIT env var still works for opt-in changes.
- No risk on benchmarks/profiling (no measured impact at depths > 1000).
- May want to add a stats counter for 'minimization depth limit hits' to monitor whether the limit is ever reached.

Tests:
  test_minimize_depth_limit_default_matches_kissat
  test_minimize_depth_limit_can_be_overridden

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows no measurable difference on benchmarks/profiling. On instances with deep reason chains (if any in broader suite), runtime should improve.

Larger project role: closes Gap 10 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Low-risk alignment fix; reduces tail risk of pathological minimization on instances not in the current suite.

title: Implement focused-mode phase cycling diversification (every 8 mode switches)
description:
Task class: search diversification. Implements kissat's periodic phase polarity flip in focused mode.

Background: Kissat's kissat_decide_phase (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/decide.c:178-187):
  if (!solver->stable) {
    switch ((solver->statistics.switched >> 1) & 7) {
      case 1: res = INITIAL_PHASE; break;
      case 3: res = -INITIAL_PHASE; break;
    }
  }

Every 8 mode switches in focused mode, kissat alternates between using the default initial phase (false) and its inverse (true) for ALL phase decisions. This is forced diversification to escape locked-in phase patterns.

Solver 11 pick_branch_phase (src/main.rs:3899-3932) implements legacy/saved/target/best policies but has no cycling diversification. Phase choices are deterministic given the saved/target/best state.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 8. Indirect — investigations of mp1 (DEEPER_FINDINGS.md Phase 2) showed solver 11 and A_default match search trajectories exactly through 400k conflicts then diverge in the final 5%. This 'phase-boundary chaos' is what diversification is supposed to escape.

Proposed change: in pick_branch_phase or its caller, add a periodic phase-flip mode when focused-stable is active. Every 8 mode switches:
- Mode switch #1, #9, #17, ...: use INITIAL_PHASE (false) for all decisions
- Mode switch #3, #11, #19, ...: use -INITIAL_PHASE (true) for all decisions
- Other switches: fall through to normal saved/target/best policy

Implementation notes:
- Need a counter for mode_switches (already exists as self.mode_switches)
- Modify pick_branch_phase to check (mode_switches >> 1) & 7 == 1 or == 3
- Add SAT_PHASE_CYCLE=on flag (default off initially)
- Stats: phase_cycle_used

Tests:
  test_phase_cycle_uses_initial_at_switch_1
  test_phase_cycle_uses_inverse_at_switch_3
  test_phase_cycle_falls_through_when_disabled

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_VMTF=on SAT_PHASE_CYCLE=on tests whether phase cycling helps mp1-like phase-boundary instances on the broader suite.

Larger project role: closes Gap 8 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Companion to Gap 7 (random decisions) — together provide kissat's two main diversification mechanisms inside focused mode. Likely a small per-instance impact but composes safely with VMTF.

title: Audit per-reason glue-histogram contributions in mark_learned_clause_recent for percentile bias
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic bug. Affects the lbd-tiered reduction tier thresholds, which are derived from this histogram.

Background: src/main.rs:5263-5265 inside `mark_reason_literals_for_analysis`:

    if LBD_META && self.reduce_policy == ReducePolicy::LbdTiered {
        self.mark_learned_clause_recent(clause_idx);
    }

`mark_learned_clause_recent` (src/main.rs:2151-2162) does two things: (1) writes `used_recently = max(used_recently, 1)`, and (2) calls `record_current_mode_glue_use(self.learnt_lbd(clause_idx))`. The second call increments BOTH `focused_glue_recent` / `stable_glue_recent` (the tier-limit driver) and `stats.focused_glue_used` / `stats.stable_glue_used` (cumulative reporting), via two separate `increment_glue_histogram` calls (src/main.rs:2196-2210).

`compute_tier_limits_from_histogram` (src/main.rs:4918-4936) computes tier 1 (50th percentile) and tier 2 (90th percentile) from `focused_glue_recent` / `stable_glue_recent`. The thresholds determine which learned clauses are evictable.

The mark-recent call fires once per learned-clause REASON walked in the UIP loop. A clause used as a reason 50 times contributes 50 entries to the histogram, biasing the percentiles toward the LBD of frequently-reused (hot) reasons. Hot reasons tend to have low LBD (that is why they are reused), so the 50/90 percentiles drift downward over time. The tier-2 cutoff slides toward smaller glue values, meaning more newly-learned clauses are classified into tier 2/3 and become eviction candidates the moment budget pressure appears.

This is structurally different from the perf optimization in SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.9 (which batches the writes). Even after batching, the same number of histogram increments fire — only the cache locality changes. The bias remains.

Two questions to answer before fixing:

1. Is per-reason recording intentional (Kissat does count "uses" in its tier statistics) or accidental? Cross-reference: Kissat's `kissat_used_glue` is updated on clause creation and clause USE in conflict analysis, so some bias IS intentional. The Rust code may be matching Kissat. Confirm by inspecting Kissat's MOREREASONS and TIER1 / TIER2 code.

2. If intentional, is the magnitude correct? The Rust port may be double-counting due to the two separate histogram writes in `record_current_mode_glue_use`, or under-counting due to the gates in `mark_learned_clause_recent`.

Goal: depending on the audit, either (a) gate the histogram write so it fires once per unique reason per conflict (use the existing `scratch_seen` mark to deduplicate), or (b) keep current behavior but document it explicitly in CONFIG_SCHEMA / FEATURES and add a counter that exposes the bias so future triage can see it.

Implementation notes for option (a):
- Split mark_learned_clause_recent into two helpers: `mark_used_recently` (writes used_recently, called per-reason) and `record_reason_glue_for_histogram` (records to histogram, called only when scratch_seen flips from 0->stamp the first time for that reason). The deduplication is free because `scratch_seen` is already updated in `mark_clause_literals_for_analysis`.
- Alternatively, record glue at the OUTER conflict only (count distinct learnt-clause reasons via a small scratch list collected during the UIP walk), then commit once at conflict completion. This dovetails with SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.9 batching.

Implementation notes for option (b):
- Add `stats.focused_reason_glue_recordings` / `stats.stable_reason_glue_recordings` separate from `focused_glue_used` / `stable_glue_used` so cumulative-glue artifacts distinguish "new clause created" from "reason reused."
- Document the bias in src/main.rs comment block above `record_current_mode_glue_use`.

Tests:
- test_glue_histogram_deduplicated_per_conflict (option a only)
- test_tier_thresholds_stable_under_repeated_reason_use (a regression test that confirms thresholds do not drift to 1/1 under pathological reuse)
- existing LBD-tiered tier-limit tests must pass

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered. Counters: focused_tier1_glue_limit, focused_tier2_glue_limit, stable_tier1_glue_limit, stable_tier2_glue_limit, learned_kept_tier1/2/3. Compare per-instance tier limits before/after fix. Expected: tier limits stop drifting toward (1, 2) and stabilize at the true distribution of newly-learned clause LBDs.

Risk IDs: R3 (learned-clause correctness), R5 (search trajectory). Rollback: restore current per-reason histogram write.
acceptance_criteria: Histogram contribution semantics are explicitly chosen and documented; tier 1/2 thresholds no longer drift toward minimum floors under high-reuse workloads in a regression test; cargo test and smoke pass; lbd-tiered profile benchmark shows tier-limit stats matching the documented intent.
notes: Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review (second pass). Distinct from SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.9, which addresses the perf cost of these writes. This bead addresses the semantic question: should they happen at all per-reason.

title: Gate level-EMA updates behind restart_block_margin > 0
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:3673-3684 update_restart_ema unconditionally updates both LBD and level moving averages:

    self.restart_fast_lbd.update(lbd);
    self.restart_slow_lbd.update(lbd);
    self.restart_fast_level.update(level);
    self.restart_slow_level.update(level);

The level EMAs are read only by restart_blocked_by_level_ema (src/main.rs:3695-3701), which is itself gated by restart_block_margin > 0.0. Default restart_block_margin is 0.0 (DEFAULT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN at src/config.rs:19). The 1.13 / 1.14 test runs confirmed margin=1.4 regressed the profile suite, so the default is and will likely remain 0.0. Every kissat-ema conflict therefore pays two MovingAverage::update calls — including the initialized branch + saturating arithmetic — purely to feed code that is off.

Goal: skip restart_fast_level / restart_slow_level updates when restart_block_margin == 0.0.

Implementation notes:
- update_restart_ema can early-return after the LBD updates if restart_block_margin <= 0.0 (treat negative as off).
- The level EMAs are also reset by reset_mode_sensitive_averages (src/main.rs:3557-3562). Leave that path alone — the reset is cheap and keeping it consistent avoids stale values if the user toggles the margin mid-run via SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY_ALLOW_OVERRIDES.
- The blocker stat restarts_blocked_by_level only fires when the margin is on, so its count remains correct (zero when off).

Tests:
- test_update_restart_ema_skips_level_when_block_margin_zero
- test_update_restart_ema_updates_level_when_block_margin_positive
- existing EMA-restart tests must continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema (default margin = 0). perf stat: instructions/cycle around note_kissat_ema_conflict. Expected: small but measurable IPC improvement on conflict-heavy instances when kissat-ema is enabled.

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path layout). Rollback: remove the guard.
acceptance_criteria: restart_fast_level / restart_slow_level are not updated on the kissat-ema path when restart_block_margin == 0.0. cargo test and smoke pass. restarts_blocked_by_level remains 0 in default kissat-ema runs.
notes: Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. Cheap independent change, no interactions with other 5b2.2.18.* beads.

title: Differentiate Tier 2 (high-LBD) from Tier 1 in reduce_candidate eviction filter
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic. Related to [1.3] LBD-tiered reduction (5b2.2.5, closed).

Background: src/main.rs:4980-4989 in Solver::reduce_candidate has identical filter arms for tier 1 and tier 2:

    1 => { if !over_budget || meta.used_recently > 0 { return None; } }
    _ => { if !over_budget || meta.used_recently > 0 { return None; } }

Tier 0 (low LBD) is gated to emergency. Tier 1 (mid LBD ≤ tier2_max_glue) and tier 2 (high LBD) are filtered with the same predicate. The candidate sort at src/main.rs:5013-5020 then orders by LBD descending, so tier 2 clauses come out first in the eviction order — but only if a candidate set was built in the first place. When !over_budget the candidate set is empty for tier 1 *and* tier 2; nothing gets evicted regardless of glue. The conflict-count reduce trigger then only ages used_recently and the high-LBD pool grows unbounded between budget events.

Kissat treats tier 3 (high-LBD) as evictable on the scheduled reduce regardless of strict budget pressure. The current shape effectively collapses the tier 1/2 distinction the comments and stats imply.

Goal: make tier 2 evictable on scheduled reductions even when !over_budget, while tier 1 keeps the !over_budget protection. Suggested shape:

    1 => { if !over_budget || meta.used_recently > 0 { return None; } }
    _ => { if meta.used_recently > 0 { return None; } }

This preserves the used_recently protection (a clause used since the last reduce stays) but lets tier 2 enter the candidate pool every scheduled reduction, not only emergency reductions.

Implementation notes:
- src/main.rs:4949-4998 is reduce_candidate; change the tier-2 arm only.
- record_lbd_tier_kept at src/main.rs:5055-5070 maps tier 0/1/2 to learned_kept_tier1/2/3; verify the counter wiring still makes sense after the change.
- Verify reclassify_live_learned_clause_tiers + retier_current_mode_from_glue_histogram (src/main.rs:4906-4940) keep producing tier 2 as the high-LBD bucket.
- Watch for over-eviction: with the per-mode tier limits from 5b2.2.31, tier-2 cutoff is set at the 90% glue percentile. The change makes 10% of recent learned clauses always evictable on schedule. This is the intent.

Tests:
- test_reduce_candidate_tier2_evictable_when_not_over_budget
- test_reduce_candidate_tier1_protected_when_not_over_budget
- existing LBD-tiered reduce-DB tests must continue to pass (learned_kept_tier1/2/3 counters may change distribution)

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered. Counters: learned_kept_tier1/2/3, reduce_db_calls, learned_literals, conflicts. Expected: lower tier3 retention, similar tier1/2 retention, no PAR-2 regression on the lbd-tiered path. Worst-case: over-eviction could lose useful glue-12 clauses; if so, add a 'tier 2 still needs used_recently == 0' check (currently kept) and reject.

Risk IDs: R3 (learned-clause correctness via aggressive eviction), R5 (search trajectory). Rollback: restore the original tier-2 arm.
acceptance_criteria: Tier 2 clauses are evictable on scheduled reductions, tier 1 retains its !over_budget protection. learned_kept_tier3 counter decreases on LBD-tiered runs. cargo test and smoke pass. No PAR-2 regression on the lbd-tiered path on search-core / profiling.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. The bead 5b2.2.31 closed with per-mode tier limits but did not change the filter arm shape, so this is the remaining piece.
Narrower than SAT-playground-qmz (kissat-style fraction-based deletion). qmz replaces the entire over-budget gate with kissat's per-pass fraction policy; this bead only differentiates tier-2 from tier-1 within the existing over-budget gate. If qmz lands, this becomes redundant. Demoted to P4 as alternative-implementation track that should be considered only if qmz is rejected.

title: [1.14x] Gate DRAT proof clause-sort behind canonical-output flag
description:
Task class: performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: ProofLog::write_clause_line in src/main.rs:742-761 sorts every emitted clause:

    stream.scratch.clear();
    stream.scratch.extend_from_slice(clause);
    stream.scratch.sort_unstable_by(|&lhs, &rhs| {
        lhs.unsigned_abs().cmp(&rhs.unsigned_abs()).then_with(|| lhs.cmp(&rhs))
    });

This runs per learned-clause addition AND per deletion. For 1M learned clauses with ~30 literals each, that is ~150M comparisons inside proof I/O. The sort canonicalizes literal order so the file is byte-deterministic regardless of internal processing order — useful for tools/ci_reproducibility.sh from plan 0.9.

But:
- Plan 0.9 only requires "bitwise-identical proof file when SAT_PROOF is on." That holds as long as the solver itself is deterministic; the sort guards against non-determinism in conflict-analysis literal order, but the existing reproducibility CI gate would catch that anyway.
- DRAT consumers (drat-trim, cake_lpr) do not require sorted literals.
- The reproducibility gate is a CI guarantee, not a per-run requirement; production benchmark runs pay the cost unnecessarily.

Goal: gate the sort behind a new SAT_PROOF_CANONICAL flag (default on, off for benchmark runs). Or, after confirming conflict-analysis literal order is deterministic, drop the sort entirely and verify the reproducibility CI gate still passes byte-comparison.

Implementation notes:
- Add SAT_PROOF_CANONICAL to SolverConfig + CONFIG_SCHEMA per the plan 0.3 contract.
- Default on. ci_solver11_fast.sh and ci_reproducibility.sh keep it on. Benchmark scripts (tools/bench.sh search-core et al.) set it off.
- When off, write_clause_line emits literals in the order conflict-analysis produced them.
- Verify that drat-trim verification still passes on all smoke UNSAT instances with the flag off.

Tests:
- test_drat_canonical_on_produces_byte_identical_proof_with_baseline
- test_drat_canonical_off_still_verifies_with_drat_trim
- test_drat_canonical_default_is_on_for_back_compat
- test_ci_reproducibility_gate_passes_with_canonical_on

Benchmark gate: proof-on UNSAT-heavy instances (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500, div-mitern172, sqrt-mitern171, brocard_problem_large) with SAT_PROOF=drat SAT_PROOF_CANONICAL=off vs baseline. Counters: proof_sec, proof_bytes_written. Expected: small but measurable proof_sec reduction on UNSAT-heavy classes; no model/proof correctness change.

Skip rule: if a measured PAR-2 improvement is below noise, leave the flag in place as a future option but do not change defaults.

Risk IDs: R8 (proof correctness). Rollback: re-enable sort unconditionally.

title: Tune or reject Glucose restart level blocker margin
description:
Background: SAT-playground-5b2.2.38 implemented a Glucose-style decision-level EMA blocker for SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema, controlled by SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN. During validation on 2026-05-22, the proposed 1.4 margin was unsafe on benchmarks/profiling: blocker-disabled Kissat-EMA solved 9/11 with PAR-2 2192.333, while blocker-on at 1.4 solved 8/11 with PAR-2 2474.284 and introduced a Timetable timeout. Default solver behavior remains safe because SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN now defaults to 0, which disables the blocker.

Goal: decide whether the level blocker should be tuned, made mode-specific, combined only with other restart policy changes, or rejected.

Implementation context: the code path lives in solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs via restart_blocked_by_level_ema and note_kissat_ema_conflict; config lives in SolverConfig as restart_block_margin and CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv as SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN.

Constraints: do not enable the blocker by default unless it passes profile/discriminating/regression-guard gates without lost solved instances. Preserve legacy-luby default behavior and pre-existing kissat-ema behavior when SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN=0.

Acceptance criteria: run a small parameter sweep around plausible margins such as 1.2, 1.4, 1.8, 2.5, and disabled; record per-instance solved counts, PAR-2, blocked-restart counters from JSON_STATS or trace_full, and top wins/regressions. Promote only if no status regressions and robust improvement over disabled Kissat-EMA; otherwise leave default disabled and mark the blocker rejected or parked.

Testing expectations: cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, explicit SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN=<candidate> smoke, and profile benchmark comparisons against disabled blocker.

Larger project role: prevents future agents from assuming the implemented blocker is ready for Phase 1 promotion; it must be evidence-tuned or intentionally rejected before the Phase 1 gate.
notes:
Deep investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 3 sweep H1/H4) adds new evidence specifically on the 10-instance refresh (benchmarks/profiling/) under SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered.

Prior decision (2026-05-22, this bead) rejected SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4 on the 11-instance suite because it cost a Timetable timeout and bumped PAR-2 from 2192 to 2474. That test was with C_lbd_ema (kissat-ema only, no lbd-tiered).

New evidence on the 10-instance refresh with E_lbd_ema_tiered + BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4 (H4):
- case9: TIMEOUT (E alone) -> SAT 195s (E + BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4) — RESCUED
- battleship: 188s (E alone) -> 105s (E + BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4) — IMPROVED
- Kakuro: 168s (E alone) -> 76s (E + BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4) — IMPROVED
- sudoku: 154s -> 171s (regression -11%)
- REGRandom: 202s -> TIMEOUT (regression)
- Iter30: 18s -> 17s (similar)
- mp1: TIMEOUT -> TIMEOUT (no rescue — chaos failure, not blocker-related)

On the 10-instance suite, H4 solves 5/7 critical SAT instances vs C alone (TIMEOUTs on 3) and vs E alone (TIMEOUTs on 2). The block_margin=1.4 setting specifically helps in COMBINATION with lbd-tiered, which the original sweep did not test.

H1 (C_lbd_ema + BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4, no lbd-tiered) gives Kakuro 73.6s — the BEST kakuro time of all 7+7=14 tested configs (vs A 217s, -66%).

Recommendation: re-test SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN=1.4 specifically in combination with SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered on the current profiling suite, not in isolation. The blocker's value emerges when it suppresses EMA restarts long enough for lbd-tiered's kept clauses to influence the trajectory. Promote only if the new combination passes regression guards on the 10-instance suite.
AnalyzeSAT 2026-05-25 side-01 adds current evidence: C_lbd_ema (SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema) returned UNKNOWN on mp1, battleship, and case9 where A_default solved. A focused mp1 sweep with SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN=1.2/1.4/1.6/2.0 under 115s wall limit rescued zero rows: all UNKNOWN. Evidence: log/analyzesat-2026-05-25-side-01/sweep_restart_margin_mp1.csv. Conclusion: margin tuning alone does not fix the single-mode EMA failure; see SAT-playground-5b2.2.58 for the broader restart execution-model gap.

title: Adaptive variable activity decay per search mode
description:
Task class: performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: solver/11-kissat-port currently uses a single constant variable activity decay rate (activity_decay in src/main.rs; bump_variable_activity at main.rs:3219 and decay_variable_activity at main.rs:3235). Modern Glucose / CaDiCaL / Kissat differentiate decay by phase: focused mode uses a faster decay (more recency bias) and stable mode uses a slower decay (longer memory). Without this, the focused/stable mode scaffold (5b2.2.12) cannot fully exploit its theoretical advantage on SAT-heavy versus UNSAT-heavy classes.

Goal: split activity_decay into per-mode constants (focused_activity_decay, stable_activity_decay) configurable via SAT_VAR_DECAY_FOCUSED / SAT_VAR_DECAY_STABLE. Default to Kissat-style values (e.g. focused=0.95, stable=0.99). On mode switch, also recompute activity_inc consistent with the new decay so subsequent bumps stay normalized.

Implementation notes:
- Add the two config fields (CONFIG_SCHEMA row, FEATURES.csv if user-visible).
- Switch active decay constant inside maybe_switch_search_mode (alongside the existing EMA reset and heap refresh).
- Keep behavior unchanged when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=single (use the legacy constant).
- Counters: decay_switches, current_var_decay in trace_full.

Tests:
- test_focused_uses_focused_decay
- test_stable_uses_stable_decay
- test_mode_switch_updates_decay_constant
- test_single_mode_unaffected_by_per_mode_decay_config

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable. Compare conflicts, decisions, learned LBD distribution, and PAR-2; expect modest improvement on SAT-heavy classes (Timetable, battleship) without UNSAT regression.

Risk IDs: same activity/heap-trajectory risk family as 5b2.2.13 (VMTF) and 5b2.2.12.

title: [A.4] Blocked Clause Elimination (BCE)
description:
Parking-lot experiment generated from Appendix A.4. Keep parked until milestone triage satisfies its unpark trigger.

Source: plan/solver-11-plan.md:6137

## Appendix A.4 Blocked Clause Elimination (BCE)

- **Intent**: delete clauses blocked by a literal whose resolvents are tautological.
- **Unpark trigger**: profile evidence that gate-aware BVE leaves ≥5% of original clauses removable by BCE on circuit-heavy instances, and FormulaEditTxn + extension replay have ≥1 month of clean milestone runs.
- **Risk**: SAT model reconstruction does not always preserve original-clause satisfaction; needs a `BlockedClause { clause, blocking_lit }` ExtensionEntry variant with witness-flip semantics and oracle coverage. BCE must stay disabled for SAT-output runs until reconstruction is proven.
- **Dependencies on unpark**: 2.1, 2.1a, 2.2, 0.6.
acceptance_criteria: Parking/reference acceptance: do not implement the parked feature directly from this bead. title: [M.0] Milestone triage and feature-retirement discipline
description:
Source: plan/solver-11-plan.md:5878

# 6. Milestones

The numbers below are directional targets, not absolute promises. Use them to catch obvious stagnation or regressions.

| Milestone | After tasks | Target full-set PAR-2 direction | Target discriminating direction |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 0.x | reference | reference |
| LBD + tiered reduce + DB/GC policy | 1.1–1.3a | meaningful drop | roughly −10% |
| EMA + phase + binary | 1.4–1.8 | larger drop | roughly −20% to −25% |
| Mode/VMTF/minimize/rephase + advanced candidates | 1.9–1.12a | SAT-side gains | roughly −25% to −35% |
| Guarded chrono + throughput | 1.13–1.15 | class-specific gains | no regression, selective wins |
| Vivification + FLP + HBR | 2.0–2.5 | major UNSAT/preprocess gains | roughly −40% to −45% |
| BVE scheduling + gate extraction + local checker + gate-aware BVE | 2.6, 2.10–2.11 | targeted circuit/preprocess shrink | roughly −45% to −55% |
| BSR/subsumption + selected binary rewrites | 2.9, 2.8, selected 2.12 | close remaining preprocess gaps | within striking distance of Kissat on targeted classes |
| Default hardening | after 1.15 or 2.16 baseline-candidate | no new speed target | no correctness, replay, proof/model, or documentation gaps |

If these targets do not move, inspect counters before adding more features.

Milestone triage requirement:

```text
After every milestone, write `log/<milestone>/triage.md` with:
  - top 10 regressions
  - top 10 wins
  - lost solved instances
  - newly solved instances
  - status/proof/model failures
  - dominant bottleneck category per hard instance:
      search-trajectory
      propagation-throughput
      learned-clause-quality
      restart/phase-policy
      preprocessing-shrink
      occurrence-list-cost
      proof-throughput
      memory/GC
      benchmark-noise
  - recommended next two beads tasks
  - tasks to defer or delete
  - explicit keep/tune/revert decision for every feature added since the previous milestone
  - profile changes accepted or rejected
  - config flags to remove from candidate profiles
  - holdout result summary
  - whether observed PAR-2 delta exceeds measured noise/confidence band
```

Do not start a new major feature family after a milestone miss until triage identifies why the previous family missed and makes a keep/tune/revert decision for each feature in the missed milestone.

If a feature remains experimental for two milestones without a named benchmark-family win, remove it from the active DAG and move it to Appendix A.

Feature retirement rule:

```text
When a feature is parked after implementation:
  - remove it from non-experimental profile defaults
  - mark FEATURES.csv maturity=ParkingLot
  - keep or remove the code based on maintenance cost:
      * keep code only if tests still run and the feature remains useful for diagnostics
      * delete code if it creates capability, proof, model, or config complexity
  - remove runnable env snippets from README
  - keep a replay artifact showing why it was parked
  - add a reactivation condition naming the benchmark family or counter signal needed
```

---

title: [G.3] Revised high-level sequence and deviation policy
description:
Source: plan/solver-11-plan.md:6175

# 13. Revised high-level sequence and deviation policy

The revised project sequence is:

```text
0. fork baseline, write BASELINE_LOCK.raw.txt, then generate BASELINE_LOCK.txt after benchmark tooling exists
1. extract architecture boundaries without behavior change
2. harden config, config replay, stats, parser/output, typed output contracts, limits, local CI, and benchmark comparison
3. create benchmark manifests, proof-off/proof-on scorecards, profiling scripts, and hot-path observability
4. add brute-force + metamorphic + differential testing plus formula-edit replay harness placeholder
5. create reason/binary-clause scaffold and closure-based temporary-assumption context
6. fix heap/decision eligibility and deterministic tie-breaking
7. implement LBD, learned DB policy, clause database/GC policy, EMA restarts, and phase policies
8. enable binary fast path using stable binary IDs
9. evaluate Phase 1 profiles
10. add proof deletions, proof completeness state, proof-obligation matrix, watch/GC rebuild policy, debug generation checks, ModelEffect classification, and two-phase buffered/preflighted formula-edit transactions
11. define the model-extension journal and replay contract before destructive simplification
12. add vivification + probing/HBR
13. add gate extraction, local implied-clause/RUP checking, and soundness-checked gate-aware BVE before any ELS experiment
14. improve BSR/subsumption, transitive reduction, RCheck, and selected binary rewrites
15. certify Phase 2 infrastructure, retire weak features, and compare replayable candidate profiles
16. keep ELS, BCE, walking, and sweep parked unless triage proves they are the next bottleneck
```

The plan is a strong starting point, not a prison.

Allowed deviations:

```text
- Reorder tasks if dependencies are fake and the new order has a written reason.
- Skip optional tasks that do not pay for themselves.
- Add a missing Kissat/CaDiCaL-style feature when a benchmark class reveals a gap.
- Pair prerequisite tasks with dependent tasks when the prerequisite is not expected to win alone.
- Update benchmark sets when new logs reveal better representatives.
```

Required when deviating:

```text
- update the DAG
- update feature flags and task dependencies
- add or update tests
- record why the deviation was made
- preserve proof/model/watcher invariants
- update profile-promotion and risk-register notes when applicable
```

End of synthesized plan.

title: [G.2] Risk register, sentinel tests, and rollback triggers
description:

## 8.1 Risk register, sentinel tests, and rollback triggers

Every beads task that touches a risk area must name the applicable risk IDs.

| Risk ID | Risk | Sentinel tests / counters | Rollback trigger | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | SAT model reconstruction failure | brute-force oracle, metamorphic tests, original-CNF model check | any SAT assignment fails original CNF | disable transformation or add extension entry |
| R2 | UNSAT proof invalidity | smoke proofs, generated UNSAT fuzz, proof add/delete unit tests | any proof verification failure | revert or keep feature proof-off only |
| R3 | stale watcher reads deleted/rewritten clause | invariant mode, watcher rebuild tests, propagation differential tests | panic, wrong status, or stale watcher counter explosion | use formula-edit transaction and rebuild watchers |
| R4 | reason corruption after GC or binary deletion | reason expansion tests, conflict-analysis oracle, GC reference rewrite tests | reason points to deleted/moved clause | centralize ReasonRef rewrite |
| R5 | non-decision variable re-enters heap/VMTF | heap/VMTF decision eligibility tests | eliminated/frozen var selected | single decision_var gate on all insertion paths |
| R6 | benchmark overfit | regression-guards, category PAR-2, paired benchmark report | lost solved instance or category regression beyond noise | keep feature off by default or profile-specific |
| R7 | memory blowup | learned_lits_final, original_lits_after_preprocess, RSS if available | memory or extension stack grows faster than solved-count/PAR-2 benefit | add budget/GC threshold, extension-memory cap, or revert |
| R10 | binary-clause explosion | binary_clauses_final, binary_implication_edges_final, binary_stale_skips | HBR/transitive/gate passes add many binaries without propagation/search benefit | add binary budget, stronger dedup, or keep HBR/transitive off |
| R11 | extension-stack blowup | extension_entries, extension_bytes_estimated, model_replay_steps | model reconstruction dominates SAT output or memory | disable destructive simplification by extension budget |
| R12 | proof-size blowup | proof_bytes_written, proof_added_literals, proof_deleted_literals | proof-on profile regresses while proof-off wins | keep feature proof-off/experimental or adjust proof logging/buffering |
| R8 | nondeterminism masks regressions | fixed SAT_SEED, config_hash, repeated runs, ci_reproducibility.sh | same config produces different status or large unexplained deltas | isolate randomness and log seed |

## 8.1 Risk register, sentinel tests, and rollback triggers

Every beads task that touches a risk area must name the applicable risk IDs.

| Risk ID | Risk | Sentinel tests / counters | Rollback trigger | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | SAT model reconstruction failure | brute-force oracle, metamorphic tests, original-CNF model check | any SAT assignment fails original CNF | disable transformation or add extension entry |
| R2 | UNSAT proof invalidity | smoke proofs, generated UNSAT fuzz, proof add/delete unit tests | any proof verification failure | revert or keep feature proof-off only |
| R3 | stale watcher reads deleted/rewritten clause | invariant mode, watcher rebuild tests, propagation differential tests | panic, wrong status, or stale watcher counter explosion | use formula-edit transaction and rebuild watchers |
| R4 | reason corruption after GC or binary deletion | reason expansion tests, conflict-analysis oracle, GC reference rewrite tests | reason points to deleted/moved clause | centralize ReasonRef rewrite |
| R5 | non-decision variable re-enters heap/VMTF | heap/VMTF decision eligibility tests | eliminated/frozen var selected | single decision_var gate on all insertion paths |
| R6 | benchmark overfit | regression-guards, category PAR-2, paired benchmark report | lost solved instance or category regression beyond noise | keep feature off by default or profile-specific |
| R7 | memory blowup | learned_lits_final, original_lits_after_preprocess, RSS if available | memory or extension stack grows faster than solved-count/PAR-2 benefit | add budget/GC threshold, extension-memory cap, or revert |
| R10 | binary-clause explosion | binary_clauses_final, binary_implication_edges_final, binary_stale_skips | HBR/transitive/gate passes add many binaries without propagation/search benefit | add binary budget, stronger dedup, or keep HBR/transitive off |
| R11 | extension-stack blowup | extension_entries, extension_bytes_estimated, model_replay_steps | model reconstruction dominates SAT output or memory | disable destructive simplification by extension budget |
| R12 | proof-size blowup | proof_bytes_written, proof_added_literals, proof_deleted_literals | proof-on profile regresses while proof-off wins | keep feature proof-off/experimental or adjust proof logging/buffering |
| R8 | nondeterminism masks regressions | fixed SAT_SEED, config_hash, repeated runs, ci_reproducibility.sh | same config produces different status or large unexplained deltas | isolate randomness and log seed |

| R13 | proof-checker version drift | proof_checker, proof_checker_version in JSON_STATS; checker SHA pinned in BASELINE_LOCK.txt | proof verification disagrees across `drat-trim`/`lrat-check` versions, or local-vs-CI checker output diverges | pin checker binaries (SHA + commit) and record `proof_checker_version` on every proof-on run; refuse to promote when CI cannot reproduce the local checker verdict |

```text
  - results.csv when benchmarks run
  - validation.jsonl when solver outputs are validated

```

This avoids half-implemented features with no test surface.

Allowed task classes:

```text
docs-only:
  - PLAN.md, README.md, FEATURES.md commentary only
  - gate: validate_solver11_plan.py

tooling-only:
  - benchmark/report/validator scripts with no solver behavior change

  - SolverConfig, CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv, FEATURES.csv, replay parsing
  - gate: cargo test, config validation tests, smoke tests

  - any task claiming speed, allocation, proof-throughput, or propagation improvement

```

Task ordering rule:

```text
- dependencies, not lexical task IDs, define execution order
- suffix IDs such as 0.0a, 1.0a, 2.1a, and 2.16a are valid

```

title: [G.0] Global acceptance criteria and invariants
description:
Source: plan/solver-11-plan.md:32 and :221

These standing rules govern every implementation bead.

# 1. Goals, non-goals, and global acceptance criteria

## 1.1 Goals

1. Reach Kissat-class wall-clock performance on `benchmarks/profiling/`, the fixed discriminating set, and eventually the full SC-2025-style 100-instance set.
2. Preserve SAT assignment output against the original input CNF, not merely the simplified residual formula.
3. Preserve DRAT-correct UNSAT proof generation end-to-end.
4. Keep changes incremental enough that a bad search trajectory, proof bug, watcher bug, or model-reconstruction bug can be isolated quickly.
5. Produce enough instrumentation that performance decisions are based on counters, not vibes.
6. Ship user-meaningful profiles with clear behavior:
   - `baseline`: solver-10-equivalent compatibility (search=Safe, preprocess=Off).
   - `default`: safe default candidate composed of Validated search + Conservative preprocess; subsumes the older `search-conservative` / `inprocess-conservative` intents.
   - `fast`: target post-Phase-2 profile composed of Strong search + GateAware preprocess; subsumes the older `search-strong` / `inprocess-gate-aware` intents.
   - `experimental`: unvalidated combinations, never used for acceptance.
7. Produce benchmark logs and config replay files that allow independent reruns of promoted defaults.
8. Maintain separate proof-off and proof-on scorecards so proof-throughput regressions do not hide behind proof-off wins.

## 1.1a User-facing deliverables

At the end of each phase, produce:

```text
solver/11-kissat-port/README.md:
  - supported profiles
  - exact run.sh contract
  - proof behavior
  - SAT model guarantee
  - known disabled experimental features
  - example commands for each profile
  - expected files in out_dir for SAT, UNSAT, UNKNOWN, and parse failure
  - exit-code/status-file behavior
  - proof-on/proof-off examples
  - config replay example

log/<phase>/summary.md:
  - promoted profile
  - config replay file
  - solved count and PAR-2 vs baseline
  - proof-off scorecard
  - proof-on scorecard where applicable
  - lost solved instances, if any
  - proof/model validation status
```

## 1.2 Non-goals for this plan

- Parallel or portfolio solving.
- IPASIR/library packaging.
- Full incremental SAT under assumptions. Keep design-compatible where cheap, but do not implement it now.
- Kissat allocator tricks such as NUMA-aware allocation or huge pages.
- A full embedded secondary solver equivalent to Kissat's kitten. The optional sweep appendix uses a bounded internal DPLL-style helper only if milestone triage proves it pays for itself.

## 1.3 Global correctness gate

Every accepted `solver-behavior`, `config-contract`, or `performance-claim` task must satisfy this gate. `docs-only` and `tooling-only` tasks use the task-class gates in section 0.7, unless they change solver behavior, result parsing, or validation semantics.

```bash
cd solver/11-kissat-port
cargo test

cd ../..
bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
```

Acceptance:

```text
- no SAT/UNSAT mismatch
- SAT assignment satisfies the original input CNF
- UNSAT smoke proofs verify through drat-trim
- no panic under invariant-check mode
- no eliminated variable re-enters the decision heap or occurrence scheduler
- no locked learned clause is deleted
```

## 1.4 Global performance gate

After task 0.5 has created generated iteration sets, every `solver-behavior` or `performance-claim` task must run at least the iteration smoke set:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/iteration/smoke-plus solver/11-kissat-port
```

Before task 0.5 exists, solver-behavior/config-contract tasks 0.0 through 0.4 use this reduced gate instead:

```bash
cd solver/11-kissat-port
cargo test

cd ../..
bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port
bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port
```

Task 0.5 is the boundary after which `benchmarks/iteration/*` is mandatory.

Search changes must also run:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/iteration/search-core solver/11-kissat-port
```

Simplification/inprocessing changes must also run:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/iteration/preprocess-core solver/11-kissat-port
```

Milestones must run:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 300 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/discriminating solver/11-kissat-port

bash tools/bench.sh -t 120 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port

bash tools/bench.sh -t 300 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/iteration/holdout solver/11-kissat-port

bash tools/bench.sh -t 600 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/profiling/minisat-simp-five solver/11-kissat-port
```

End-of-phase runs must use the full set:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 1800 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/sat-comp-2025 solver/11-kissat-port
```

## 1.5 Noise discipline

SAT search is noisy. Single wall-clock measurements are not reliable enough.

Performance acceptance rules:

```text
Promotion gate (statistical):
  - PAR-2 delta is computed paired per instance.
  - compare_bench.py reports the bootstrap 90% CI on the paired PAR-2 delta using 10_000 resamples.
  - Promotion requires: CI upper bound < 0 (improvement is significant) OR a named counter improvement that a follow-up task is expected to consume.
  - Rejection requires: CI lower bound > 0 (regression is significant) AND no offsetting counter improvement.
  - Indeterminate (CI straddles 0): acceptable only as a prerequisite task; not promotable to a default.

Per-instance robustness:
  - For search trajectory changes, run paired median of 3 on search-core (single seed; vary only solver binary).
  - For very small deltas, additionally run multi-seed A/B (SAT_SEED ∈ {0, 1, 2}) to estimate seed-vs-binary variance.
  - Per-instance minimum is allowed only for exploratory triage, never for acceptance.
- Per-instance ±10% noise is normal.
- Per-instance −50% wins are obvious and should be investigated for reusable structure.
- Never accept silent correctness regression for speed.
- Never promote a default if it loses a previously solved regression-guard instance unless milestone triage explicitly accepts that tradeoff.
- Report category PAR-2 for search-core, preprocess-core, regression-guards, proof-heavy UNSAT, and SAT-heavy trajectory instances.
- Report per-category bootstrap CIs; categories with sample size < 10 are reported with a "low-sample" annotation and cannot be the *sole* promotion evidence.
- A feature may be profile-specific when it wins one category and loses another; do not force it into baseline.
- Any newly solved hard instance must be checked for reusable structure before using it as promotion evidence.
- If a prerequisite change regresses alone but a dependent change is expected to pay for it, benchmark the pair before rejecting.
- If still regressing, revert and write a short rejection note into the beads task so the same experiment is not repeated blindly.
- The old `max(3%, two-run noise band)` heuristic is deprecated; bootstrap CIs supersede it. Cite the heuristic only when explaining historic decisions.
```

Benchmark environment sanity:

```text
- tools/bench.sh records whether CPU frequency governor, thermal throttling status, and core pinning are known.
- tools/bench.sh supports optional `--pin-core <n>` and records the pinning decision.
- tools/bench.sh runs a tiny calibration instance before benchmark timing and records calibration time.
- compare_bench.py warns if calibration time differs by more than 10% between before/after runs.
- compare_bench.py warns if the machine/environment block differs between paired runs.
```

Flaky-instance policy:

```text
- Add benchmarks/iteration/FLAKY.csv.
- An instance may be quarantined only after median-of-5 variance exceeds the measured noise band on an otherwise stable machine.
- Quarantined instances stay in stress runs but cannot be used as promotion evidence.
- Removing an instance from FLAKY.csv requires a written note and a stable median-of-5 rerun.
```

---

# 2. Code-level invariants to preserve everywhere

Keep these invariants visible while implementing every task.

```text
Assignment/trail:
  - every assigned variable appears exactly once on trail
  - decision_level[var] matches the trail frame
  - root assignments have level 0
  - propagate_head never points past trail length
  - temporary assumptions always backtrack to root before returning to normal search
  - temporary assumptions do not update saved/target/best phase unless explicitly requested
  - temporary assumptions do not enter VMTF/heap decision statistics

Reasons:
  - unassigned variables have NO_REASON
  - decision variables have NO_REASON
  - propagated variables have either a live clause reason or encoded binary reason
  - locked learned clauses cannot be deleted
  - binary reason expansion during conflict analysis is exactly the corresponding binary clause
  - no formula edit may delete a live reason clause unless it first installs a valid replacement reason or backtracks/removes that assignment safely at level 0
  - root-level reasons are treated as live reasons for deletion and GC purposes
  - deletion and GC decisions consult a freshly built ReasonPinSet rather than ad-hoc reason checks

Watchers:
  - long live clauses have two valid watches
  - binary clauses in binary_implications are also represented for proof/model/debug or have an explicit reason/proof path
  - stale deleted watchers are tolerated only if propagation checks deletion before clause use
  - in-place clause rewriting must either detach watchers first or mark watch lists dirty and make propagation skip impossible watchers
  - do not mix strict detach and dirty-watch strategies in the same mutator without an explicit contract

Clause arena:
  - header size matches literal count and extra words
  - learned clauses have activity/meta words as expected
  - original clauses have abstraction metadata only when the current mode expects it
  - LBD metadata starts in a side table; any later arena migration is one-time, atomic, and benchmark-justified
  - later metadata should use side tables unless there is a measured reason to touch arena layout again
  - GC rewrites every clause reference: watchers, reasons, learned ids, original ids, occurrence refs, and proof/model side structures
  - debug/invariant mode stores a generation for every allocated clause slot and validates every ClauseRef before dereference
  - any ClauseRef copied into side structures must be registered in a rewrite visitor or marked debug-only

Scratch / allocation:
  - propagation, conflict analysis, decision selection, and reduce-db candidate scans do not allocate in steady state
  - temporary vectors are owned by Solver scratch fields and reused
  - formula-edit transactions may allocate, but budgeted inprocessing passes must account for that cost
  - any new hot loop must state whether it allocates and which scratch buffers it uses
  - allocation-heavy prototypes stay experimental until allocation counters are flat on search-core

Occurrence lists:
  - occurrence refs are u32 unless a measured overflow risk appears
  - dirty lists are cleaned before exact scans
  - n_occ is updated on add/delete/strengthen/substitute
  - eliminated variables do not re-enter occurrence scheduling

Proof:
  - every learned clause used for UNSAT proof is logged
  - every generated resolvent needed for BVE is logged
  - every strengthened clause is logged before the old clause is deleted
  - deletion logging exists before inprocessing transformations rely on removed-clause proof context
  - proof buffering stays enabled; increase buffer capacity only after measuring proof throughput

SAT model:
  - final assignment satisfies original input CNF
  - every satisfiability-preserving deletion that can break direct SAT assignment needs an extension entry or must remain disabled for SAT-output runs
  - extension stack is applied in reverse order
  - equivalent-literal substitution records enough information to reconstruct the eliminated literal value
  - BCE remains disabled until model reconstruction is proven
  - every extension entry records its approximate literal memory cost
  - extension replay has an invariant-check mode that verifies each replay step satisfies the clauses it restores
  - transformations may be disabled by extension memory budget even if they are proof-correct

Decision eligibility:
  - eliminated/frozen variables are never decision candidates
  - heap/VMTF insertion paths check decision_var[v]
  - chronological backtracking must not reinsert or reassign non-decision variables incorrectly

Cache and layout invariants for hot paths:
  Propagation watcher entries:
    - watcher entry size <= 16 bytes (target: 8 bytes: blocker + ClauseRef)
    - watcher list is contiguous Vec<Watcher>, not Vec<Box<Watcher>>
    - blocker literal is the first field so it lives at the start of the cache line
    - if blocker miss rate exceeds 30% in profiling, revisit blocker selection before adding new propagation work

  Binary implication adjacency:
    - BinaryEdge size <= 8 bytes (target: 8 bytes: implied i32 + BinaryClauseId u32)
    - in Flat representation, edges for one literal are contiguous; offsets array fits in L2
    - propagation walks at most one cache line per binary edge in the hot path

  Clause arena access:
    - clause header (size + LBD/tier metadata) fits in 8 bytes (one word)
    - first two literals (the watched positions) follow the header so the first cache line load covers header + watchers + 1-2 more literals
    - learned-meta side tables are L2-resident for typical learned-clause counts

  Allocation rules for performance-claim tasks:
    - allocation count per 1M propagations must be reported in JSON_STATS as hot_allocations_estimated
    - any new hot path that allocates in steady state is rejected unless the task explicitly justifies it with a counter delta
```
